Rosetta is a comprehensive molecular modeling software suite primarily used for predicting and designing macromolecular structures, with a focus on proteins and protein-protein interactions. It provides tools for protein structure prediction, protein design, protein-protein docking, protein-ligand docking, loop modeling, and other computational structural biology tasks.

This overview introduces the main components and architecture of the Rosetta software suite. For more detailed information about specific subsystems, refer to the corresponding dedicated pages:
- For core data structures like Pose and Residue, see [Core Data Structures](#2)
- For energy evaluation, see [Scoring System](#3)
- For algorithms that manipulate structures, see [Protocol System](#4)
- For Python integration, see [Python Integration](#5)
- For development tools, see [Testing and Development](#6)

## Architecture Overview

Rosetta is organized into several interconnected systems that together provide a powerful framework for molecular modeling. The core of Rosetta is implemented in C++, with Python bindings provided through PyRosetta.

### High-Level Architecture

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Core Data Structures"
        Pose["Pose"]
        ResidueType["ResidueType"]
        Residue["Residue"]
        Conformation["Conformation"]
        FoldTree["FoldTree"]
        Energies["Energies"]
    end

    subgraph "Scoring System"
        ScoreFunction["ScoreFunction"]
        ScoringManager["ScoringManager"]
        EnergyMethod["EnergyMethod"]
        EnergyMethodOptions["EnergyMethodOptions"]
    end

    subgraph "Algorithm System"
        Mover["Mover"]
        Protocol["Protocol"]
        Filter["Filter"]
        SimpleMetric["SimpleMetric"]
        MoverFactory["MoverFactory"]
        FilterFactory["FilterFactory"]
    end
    
    subgraph "I/O System"
        PDB_IO["PDB I/O"]
        StructFileRep["StructFileRep"]
        PoseBuilder["PoseFromSFRBuilder"]
    end

    subgraph "Build/Script System"
        RosettaScripts["RosettaScripts"]
        PyRosetta["PyRosetta"]
        BuildSystem["Build System"]
    end

    Pose --> Conformation
    Conformation --> Residue
    Residue --> ResidueType
    Conformation --> FoldTree
    Pose --> Energies
    
    ScoreFunction --> EnergyMethod
    EnergyMethod --> EnergyMethodOptions
    ScoringManager --> ScoreFunction
    
    Mover --> Pose
    Protocol --> Mover
    Filter --> Pose
    SimpleMetric --> Pose
    MoverFactory --> Mover
    FilterFactory --> Filter
    
    PDB_IO --> StructFileRep
    StructFileRep --> PoseBuilder
    PoseBuilder --> Pose
    
    RosettaScripts --> Mover
    RosettaScripts --> Filter
    PyRosetta --> Pose
    BuildSystem --> PyRosetta

```

## Core Data Structures

At the heart of Rosetta is the `Pose` class, which represents the molecular system being modeled. A `Pose` contains:

1. A `Conformation` object that stores the geometric information (coordinates) of the molecule
2. An `Energies` object that holds the results of energy evaluations
3. `PDBInfo` for mapping between Rosetta's internal residue numbering and PDB numbering
4. A collection of `Residue` objects, each with a reference to a `ResidueType` that defines its chemical properties

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Pose Structure"
        Pose["Pose"]
        Conformation["Conformation"]
        Energies["Energies"]
        PDBInfo["PDBInfo"]
        DataCache["DataCache"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Residue System"
        Residue["Residue"]
        ResidueType["ResidueType"]
        Atom["Atom"]
        AtomType["AtomType"]
        Bond["Bond"]
    end
    
    Pose --> Conformation
    Pose --> Energies
    Pose --> PDBInfo
    Pose --> DataCache
    
    Conformation --> Residue
    Conformation --> FoldTree["FoldTree"]
    
    Residue --> ResidueType
    Residue --> Atom
    Atom --> AtomType
    Residue --> Bond
```

Sources: [source/src/protocols.3.src.settings:1-223](), [source/test/protocols.test.settings:1-125]()

## Protocol System

The protocol system is built around the concept of `Mover` objects that operate on `Pose` objects to modify them in various ways. Complex operations are composed from simpler ones through the use of `Protocol` objects that manage multiple `Mover` objects. The system uses the factory pattern extensively with `MoverFactory` and `FilterFactory` creating `Mover` and `Filter` objects based on registered creators.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Protocol Components"
        Mover["Mover"]
        Protocol["Protocol"]
        Filter["Filter"]
        TaskOperation["TaskOperation"]
        ResidueSelector["ResidueSelector"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Factory System"
        MoverFactory["MoverFactory"]
        FilterFactory["FilterFactory"]
        MoverCreator["MoverCreator"]
        FilterCreator["FilterCreator"]
        MoverRegistrator["MoverRegistrator"]
        FilterRegistrator["FilterRegistrator"]
    end
    
    MoverRegistrator --> MoverFactory
    FilterRegistrator --> FilterFactory
    
    MoverCreator --> MoverRegistrator
    FilterCreator --> FilterRegistrator
    
    MoverFactory --> Mover
    FilterFactory --> Filter
    
    Mover --> Pose["Pose"]
    Filter --> Pose
    Protocol --> Mover
    TaskOperation --> Pose
    ResidueSelector --> Pose
    
    RosettaScripts["RosettaScripts (XML Interface)"] --> Mover
    RosettaScripts --> Filter
    RosettaScripts --> TaskOperation
    RosettaScripts --> ResidueSelector
```

Sources: [source/src/protocols/init/init.MoverRegistrators.ihh:1-780](), [source/src/protocols/init/init.MoverCreators.ihh:1-177](), [source/src/protocols/init/init.FilterRegistrators.ihh:1-50](), [source/src/protocols/init/init.FilterCreators.ihh:1-50]()

## Scoring System

The scoring system evaluates the energy and quality of molecular structures. The central component is the `ScoreFunction` class, which combines multiple energy terms (each implemented as an `EnergyMethod`) with associated weights to compute a total score for a `Pose`.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Score Function"
        ScoreFunction["ScoreFunction"]
        Weights["Weights"]
        ScoreType["ScoreType Enum"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Energy Methods"
        EnergyMethod["EnergyMethod Interface"]
        FACTSEnergy["FACTS Energy"]
        VdWEnergy["Van der Waals Energy"]
        HBondEnergy["H-Bond Energy"]
        ElecEnergy["Electrostatics Energy"]
        SolvationEnergy["Solvation Energy"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Infrastructure"
        ScoringManager["ScoringManager"]
        EnergyMethodOptions["EnergyMethodOptions"]
        EnergyRegistrators["EnergyMethodRegistrators"]
        EnergyCreators["EnergyMethodCreators"]
    end
    
    ScoreFunction --> Weights
    ScoreFunction --> ScoreType
    
    ScoreType --> EnergyMethod
    EnergyMethod --> FACTSEnergy
    EnergyMethod --> VdWEnergy
    EnergyMethod --> HBondEnergy
    EnergyMethod --> ElecEnergy
    EnergyMethod --> SolvationEnergy
    
    ScoringManager --> EnergyMethod
    EnergyMethodOptions --> EnergyMethod
    EnergyRegistrators --> ScoringManager
    EnergyCreators --> EnergyRegistrators
```

Sources: [source/test/protocols.test.settings:1-125](), [source/src/protocols.3.src.settings:1-223]()

## Build System

Rosetta uses a sophisticated build system that leverages CMake, Ninja, and custom Python scripts to manage the compilation of its extensive codebase.

```mermaid
graph LR
    BuildScript["ninja_build.py"]
    CMake["CMake"]
    SrcSettings["*.src.settings files"]
    BuildSettings["build.settings"]
    Ninja["Ninja"]
    
    BuildScript --> CMake
    SrcSettings --> CMake
    BuildSettings --> CMake
    CMake --> Ninja
    Ninja --> Executables
    Ninja --> Libraries
    
    subgraph "Rosetta Components"
        Executables
        Libraries
        
        subgraph "Applications"
            CoreApps["Core Apps"]
            PilotApps["Pilot Apps"]
        end
        
        subgraph "Libraries"
            CoreLib["core.*"]
            ProtocolsLib["protocols.*"]
            BasicLib["basic.*"]
            NumericLib["numeric.*"]
            UtilityLib["utility.*"]
        end
    end
    
    PyRosettaBuild["PyRosetta/build.py"] --> PyBindingGen["Python Binding Generation"]
    PyBindingGen --> PyRosettaModule["PyRosetta Module"]
    
    Libraries --> PyRosettaBuild
```

Sources: [source/tools/build/basic.settings:1-100](), [source/src/python/PyRosetta/build.py:1-100](), [tests/benchmark/tests/build.py:1-44]()

## Applications

Rosetta includes a wide range of applications for various computational structural biology tasks:

| Category | Example Applications |
|----------|---------------------|
| Structure Prediction | AbinitioRelax, fragment_picker |
| Design | fixbb, design_minisilent, supercharge |
| Docking | docking_protocol, ligand_dock |
| Analysis | InterfaceAnalyzer, score_jd2 |
| Antibody Modeling | antibody, snugdock |
| Membrane Proteins | mp_dock, mp_transform |
| Carbohydrates | glycan_dock, pose_from_saccharide_sequence |

Applications are organized into "public" apps (stable, documented, and intended for general use) and "pilot" apps (experimental or specialized tools).

Sources: [source/src/apps.src.settings:1-67](), [source/src/pilot_apps.src.settings.all:1-100]()

## Python Integration (PyRosetta)

PyRosetta provides Python bindings to the core Rosetta C++ functionality, enabling users to write Python scripts that leverage Rosetta's powerful molecular modeling capabilities. PyRosetta is built using a combination of custom binding tools and Pybind11.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "PyRosetta Architecture"
        PyModule["PyRosetta Python Module"]
        BindingCode["C++ Binding Code"]
        BinderTool["Binder Tool"]
        RosettaConfig["rosetta.config"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Rosetta Libraries"
        CoreLib["core"]
        ProtocolsLib["protocols"]
        BasicLib["basic"]
        NumericLib["numeric"]
        UtilityLib["utility"]
    end
    
    RosettaConfig --> BinderTool
    BinderTool --> BindingCode
    BindingCode --> PyModule
    
    CoreLib --> BindingCode
    ProtocolsLib --> BindingCode
    BasicLib --> BindingCode
    NumericLib --> BindingCode
    UtilityLib --> BindingCode
    
    PyModule --> PythonScripts["Python Scripts"]
```

Sources: [source/src/python/PyRosetta/build.py:1-100](), [source/src/python/PyRosetta/rosetta.config:1-50](), [source/src/python/PyRosetta/src/pyrosetta/__init__.py:1-20](), [tests/benchmark/tests/PyRosetta.py:1-20]()

## Testing Framework

Rosetta has a comprehensive testing infrastructure that includes:

1. **Unit tests**: Test individual components in isolation
2. **Integration tests**: Test the interaction between components
3. **Scientific benchmarks**: Validate the scientific accuracy of Rosetta methods
4. **Performance benchmarks**: Measure the computational efficiency of algorithms

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Testing Framework"
        UnitTests["Unit Tests"]
        IntegrationTests["Integration Tests"]
        ScientificBenchmarks["Scientific Benchmarks"]
        PerformanceBenchmarks["Performance Benchmarks"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Test Runners"
        UnitTestRunner["test/run.py"]
        IntegrationRunner["tests/integration/integration.py"]
        BenchmarkRunner["tests/benchmark/benchmark.py"]
    end
    
    UnitTestRunner --> UnitTests
    IntegrationRunner --> IntegrationTests
    BenchmarkRunner --> ScientificBenchmarks
    BenchmarkRunner --> PerformanceBenchmarks
    
    UnitTests --> TestResults["Test Results"]
    IntegrationTests --> TestResults
    ScientificBenchmarks --> TestResults
    PerformanceBenchmarks --> TestResults
```

Sources: [source/test/run.py:1-40](), [tests/integration/integration.py:1-80](), [tests/benchmark/benchmark.py:1-60](), [tests/benchmark/tests/unit.py:1-20](), [tests/benchmark/tests/integration.py:1-115](), [tests/benchmark/tests/performance.py:1-20](), [tests/benchmark/tests/score.py:1-20]()

## Version and Release System

Rosetta uses a versioning system to track releases and changes. The version information includes git revision, branch, and other metadata.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Release Process"
        VersionScript["version.py"]

        BinaryRelease["Binary Release"]
        SourceRelease["Source Release"]
    end
    
    VersionScript --> VersionInfo["Version Information"]
    ReleasePy --> ReleasePackaging
    ReleasePackaging --> BinaryRelease
    ReleasePackaging --> SourceRelease
    VersionInfo --> ReleasePackaging
```

Sources: [source/version.py:1-20](), [tests/benchmark/tests/release.py:1-100](), [tests/benchmark/tests/__init__.py:1-100]()

## Summary

Rosetta is a highly modular, extensible software platform for molecular modeling, with particular strengths in protein structure prediction and design. Its architecture separates the representation of molecular structures (through the Pose class) from the operations that manipulate them (through Movers) and the scoring functions that evaluate them (through ScoreFunction). This separation of concerns, combined with the factory pattern for creating components and the plugin architecture for registering new functionality, makes Rosetta both powerful and extensible.

Sources: [source/src/pilot_apps.src.settings.all:1-1227](), [source/tools/build/basic.settings:1-100](), [source/src/python/PyRosetta/build.py:1-100](), [source/src/protocols/init/init.MoverRegistrators.ihh:1-780](), [source/src/protocols/init/init.MoverCreators.ihh:1-177](), [source/src/protocols/init/init.FilterRegistrators.ihh:1-50](), [source/src/protocols/init/init.FilterCreators.ihh:1-50]()

This document provides a high-level overview of the Rosetta software architecture, explaining the core components and their relationships. Rosetta is a comprehensive molecular modeling suite used for protein structure prediction, design, docking, and many other computational biology applications.

For build system details, see [Build System](#1.2).

## Core Architecture Components

Rosetta's architecture consists of several major components that work together:

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Core Data Structures"
        Pose["Pose"]
        Conformation["Conformation"]
        Residue["Residue"]
        ResidueType["ResidueType"]
        FoldTree["FoldTree"]
        Energies["Energies"]
    end

    subgraph "Scoring System"
        ScoreFunction["ScoreFunction"]
        ScoringManager["ScoringManager"]
        EnergyMethod["EnergyMethod"]
        EnergyMethodOptions["EnergyMethodOptions"]
    end

    subgraph "Protocol System"
        Mover["Mover"]
        Protocol["Protocol"]
        Filter["Filter"]
        SimpleMetric["SimpleMetric"]
        MoverFactory["MoverFactory"]
        FilterFactory["FilterFactory"]
    end
    
    subgraph "I/O System"
        PDB_IO["PDB I/O"]
        StructFileRep["StructFileRep"]
        PoseBuilder["PoseFromSFRBuilder"]
    end

    subgraph "Build/Script System"
        RosettaScripts["RosettaScripts"]
        PyRosetta["PyRosetta"]
        BuildSystem["Build System"]
    end

    Pose --> Conformation
    Conformation --> Residue
    Residue --> ResidueType
    Conformation --> FoldTree
    Pose --> Energies
    
    ScoreFunction --> EnergyMethod
    EnergyMethod --> EnergyMethodOptions
    ScoringManager --> ScoreFunction
    
    Mover --> Pose
    Protocol --> Mover
    Filter --> Pose
    SimpleMetric --> Pose
    MoverFactory --> Mover
    FilterFactory --> Filter
    
    PDB_IO --> StructFileRep
    StructFileRep --> PoseBuilder
    PoseBuilder --> Pose
    
    RosettaScripts --> Mover
    RosettaScripts --> Filter
    PyRosetta --> Pose
    BuildSystem --> PyRosetta
    
    ScoreFunction --> Pose
```

Sources: [source/src/core/conformation/Conformation.hh](), [source/src/core/pose/Pose.cc](), [source/src/core/chemical/ResidueType.hh](), [source/src/core/scoring/ScoreType.hh]()

## Core Data Structures

The central data structure in Rosetta is the `Pose` class, which represents a complete molecular structure.

### Pose and Conformation

```mermaid
graph TD
    Pose["Pose"] --> Conformation["Conformation"]
    Pose --> Energies["Energies"]
    Pose --> PDBInfo["PDBInfo"]
    Pose --> DataCache["DataCache"]
    
    Conformation --> FoldTree["FoldTree"]
    Conformation --> Residues["Residues (vector)"]
    
    Residues --> Residue1["Residue 1"]
    Residues --> Residue2["Residue 2"]
    Residues --> ResidueN["Residue n"]
    
    Residue1 --> ResidueType1["ResidueType"]
    Residue1 --> Atoms1["Atom coordinates"]
```

The `Pose` class contains:
- A `Conformation` object that stores 3D coordinates and connectivity
- An `Energies` object that stores energy values
- `PDBInfo` that contains metadata about the structure
- A `DataCache` for storing auxiliary data

The `Conformation` class manages:
- A collection of `Residue` objects
- A `FoldTree` that defines the kinematic connectivity between residues

Sources: [source/src/core/pose/Pose.cc](), [source/src/core/conformation/Conformation.cc](), [source/src/core/pose/util.cc]()

### Residue and ResidueType

```mermaid
graph TD
    Residue["Residue"] --> ResidueType["ResidueType"]
    Residue --> AtomCoordinates["Atom XYZ Coordinates"]
    
    ResidueType --> AtomTypes["Atom Types"]
    ResidueType --> Bonds["Bond Information"]
    ResidueType --> Properties["Chemical Properties"]
    ResidueType --> ICoords["Internal Coordinates"]
    ResidueType --> ChiInfo["Chi Angles Information"]
    ResidueType --> Connections["Connection Points"]
```

The `Residue` class represents a single residue (amino acid, nucleotide, ligand, etc.) and contains:
- A reference to a `ResidueType` that defines chemical properties
- The 3D coordinates of all atoms in the residue

The `ResidueType` class is immutable and defines:
- The chemical composition of a residue
- Atom types and properties
- Bond information
- Internal coordinate system
- Torsion angle (chi) definitions
- Connection points to other residues

Sources: [source/src/core/conformation/Residue.cc](), [source/src/core/chemical/ResidueType.cc]()

## Scoring System

The scoring system calculates the energy of a molecular structure through a collection of energy terms.

```mermaid
graph TD
    ScoreFunction["ScoreFunction"] --> Weights["Weights Map<ScoreType, Real>"]
    ScoreFunction --> EM_Collection["Collection of EnergyMethods"]
    
    ScoringManager["ScoringManager (Singleton)"] --> ScFxnFactory["ScoreFunction Factory"]
    ScoringManager --> EMFactory["EnergyMethod Factory"]
    
    EM_Collection --> Method1["EnergyMethod 1"]
    EM_Collection --> Method2["EnergyMethod 2"]
    EM_Collection --> MethodN["EnergyMethod n"]
    
    Method1 --> Options1["EnergyMethodOptions"]
    
    ScoreFunction -- "Evaluates" --> Pose["Pose"]
    Pose --> Energies["Energies"]
```

The scoring system consists of:
- The `ScoreFunction` class that holds weights for different energy terms
- The `Energies` class that stores calculated energy values
- Various `EnergyMethod` implementations that calculate specific energy terms
- The `ScoringManager` singleton that manages the creation of energy methods

Energy methods are registered at initialization time through the `EnergyMethodRegistrator` system, allowing for easy extension of the scoring system.

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/ScoreTypeManager.cc](), [source/src/core/scoring/ScoreType.hh](), [source/src/core/scoring/methods/EnergyMethodOptions.cc](), [source/src/core/init/init.cc]()

## Protocol System

The protocol system provides a framework for applying operations to molecular structures.

```mermaid
graph TD
    Mover["Mover (Abstract Interface)"] -- "apply(pose)" --> Pose["Pose"]
    
    Mover --> SimpleMovers["Simple Movers"]
    Mover --> ComplexMovers["Complex Movers"]
    
    Protocol["Protocol"] --> Mover1["Mover 1"]
    Protocol --> Mover2["Mover 2"]
    Protocol --> MoverN["Mover n"]
    
    Filter["Filter (Abstract Interface)"] -- "apply(pose) -> bool" --> Pose
    
    MoverFactory["MoverFactory"] -- "Creates" --> Mover
    FilterFactory["FilterFactory"] -- "Creates" --> Filter
    
    MoverRegistrator["MoverRegistrator"] -- "Registers" --> MoverFactory
    FilterRegistrator["FilterRegistrator"] -- "Registers" --> FilterFactory
```

The protocol system consists of:
- `Mover` objects that perform operations on `Pose` objects
- `Filter` objects that evaluate whether a `Pose` meets certain criteria
- `Protocol` objects that combine multiple movers and filters
- Factory classes that create movers and filters based on names
- Registration systems that populate the factories

The registration system enables a plug-in architecture where new movers and filters can be added without modifying existing code.

Sources: [source/src/protocols/init/init.MoverRegistrators.ihh](), [source/src/protocols/init/init.MoverCreators.ihh](), [source/src/protocols/init/init.FilterRegistrators.ihh](), [source/src/protocols/init/init.FilterCreators.ihh]()

## I/O System

The I/O system handles reading and writing molecular structures in various formats.

```mermaid
graph TD
    PDB_IO["PDB I/O"] -- "Read" --> StructFileRep["StructFileRep"]
    MMCIF_IO["mmCIF I/O"] -- "Read" --> StructFileRep
    MMTF_IO["MMTF I/O"] -- "Read" --> StructFileRep
    
    StructFileRep -- "Build" --> PoseBuilder["PoseFromSFRBuilder"]
    PoseBuilder -- "Create" --> Pose["Pose"]
    
    Pose -- "Convert" --> StructFileRep
    StructFileRep -- "Write" --> PDB_IO
    StructFileRep -- "Write" --> MMCIF_IO
    StructFileRep -- "Write" --> MMTF_IO
    
    SilentFile["Silent File I/O"] -- "Read/Write" --> Pose
```

The I/O system includes:
- Readers and writers for various file formats (PDB, mmCIF, MMTF, etc.)
- The `StructFileRep` class that serves as an intermediate representation
- The `PoseFromSFRBuilder` class that converts file data to a `Pose`
- A silent file format for efficient storage of many structures

Sources: [source/src/core/io/pdb/pdb_reader.cc](), [source/src/core/io/pose_from_sfr/PoseFromSFRBuilder.cc](), [source/test/core.test.settings:131-154]()

## Registration and Factory System

Rosetta uses a factory pattern extensively to create objects at runtime based on their names.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Initialization"
        StaticInit["Static Initialization"]
        Registry["Component Registration"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Factory System"
        MoverFactory["MoverFactory"]
        FilterFactory["FilterFactory"]
        ScoringManager["ScoringManager"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Creator System"
        MoverCreator["MoverCreator"]
        FilterCreator["FilterCreator"]
        EnergyMethodCreator["EnergyMethodCreator"]
    end
    
    StaticInit --> Registry
    Registry --> MoverFactory
    Registry --> FilterFactory
    Registry --> ScoringManager
    
    MoverCreator --> MoverFactory
    FilterCreator --> FilterFactory
    EnergyMethodCreator --> ScoringManager
    
    MoverFactory -- "create_by_name()" --> Mover["Mover"]
    FilterFactory -- "create_by_name()" --> Filter["Filter"]
    ScoringManager -- "create_score_function()" --> ScoreFunction["ScoreFunction"]
```

The registration and factory system consists of:
- Factory classes that maintain mappings from names to creator functions
- Creator classes that implement the creation logic for specific types
- Registrator classes that register creators with factories
- Static initialization that ensures registration happens at program startup

This system enables a modular architecture where new components can be added by simply including new source files in the build.

Sources: [source/src/core/init/init.cc](), [source/src/protocols/init/init.MoverRegistrators.ihh](), [source/src/protocols/init/init.FilterRegistrators.ihh]()

## RosettaScripts Interface

RosettaScripts is an XML-based interface to Rosetta's functionality, allowing users to combine movers and filters without writing C++ code.

```mermaid
graph TD
    RosettaScripts["RosettaScripts"] -- "Parse XML" --> XMLProtocol["XML Protocol"]
    
    XMLProtocol --> ScoreFunctions["ScoreFunctions"]
    XMLProtocol --> Movers["Movers"]
    XMLProtocol --> Filters["Filters"]
    XMLProtocol --> SimpleMetrics["SimpleMetrics"]
    XMLProtocol --> PROTOCOLS["PROTOCOLS"]
    
    ScoreFunctions -- "Create" --> ScoreFunction["ScoreFunction"]
    Movers -- "Create" --> Mover["Mover"]
    Filters -- "Create" --> Filter["Filter"]
    SimpleMetrics -- "Create" --> SimpleMetric["SimpleMetric"]
    
    PROTOCOLS --> MoverRef1["Mover Reference"]
    PROTOCOLS --> FilterRef1["Filter Reference"]
    
    MoverRef1 --> Mover
    FilterRef1 --> Filter
    
    Mover -- "Apply" --> Pose["Pose"]
    Filter -- "Evaluate" --> Pose
    SimpleMetric -- "Measure" --> Pose
    ScoreFunction -- "Score" --> Pose
```

RosettaScripts:
- Parses XML input to create and configure Rosetta components
- Uses the factory system to instantiate movers, filters, and score functions
- Assembles these components into a protocol
- Executes the protocol on input structures

The XML interface allows users to access Rosetta's functionality without writing C++ code, making complex protocols more accessible.

Sources: [source/src/protocols.3.src.settings:702-705](), [source/src/protocols/init/init.MoverCreators.ihh]()

## PyRosetta Interface

PyRosetta provides Python bindings to Rosetta, allowing scripting and interactive use of Rosetta functionality.

```mermaid
graph TD
    PyRosetta["PyRosetta"] --> PyPose["pyrosetta.Pose"]
    PyRosetta --> PyScoreFunction["pyrosetta.ScoreFunction"]
    PyRosetta --> PyMover["pyrosetta.Mover"]
    
    PyPose -- "Wraps" --> Pose["C++ Pose"]
    PyScoreFunction -- "Wraps" --> ScoreFunction["C++ ScoreFunction"]
    PyMover -- "Wraps" --> Mover["C++ Mover"]
    
    PyPose -- "Manipulate with Python" --> PythonScript["Python Scripts"]
    PythonScript -- "Process results" --> PythonAnalysis["Python Analysis"]
```

PyRosetta:
- Provides Python classes that wrap C++ Rosetta classes
- Enables interactive use of Rosetta in Python scripts and notebooks
- Allows integration with Python's scientific computing ecosystem
- Facilitates rapid prototyping and development of new protocols

Sources: [source/pilot_apps.src.settings:427-433]()

## Build System

Rosetta uses a custom build system based on CMake and Ninja, configured through specialized settings files.

```mermaid
graph LR
    BuildScript["ninja_build.py"]
    CMake["CMake"]
    SrcSettings["*.src.settings files"]
    BuildSettings["build.settings"]
    Ninja["Ninja"]
    
    BuildScript --> CMake
    SrcSettings --> CMake
    BuildSettings --> CMake
    CMake --> Ninja
    Ninja --> Executables
    Ninja --> Libraries
    
    subgraph "Rosetta Components"
        Executables
        Libraries
        
        subgraph "Applications"
            CoreApps["Core Apps"]
            PilotApps["Pilot Apps"]
        end
        
        subgraph "Libraries"
            CoreLib["core.*"]
            ProtocolsLib["protocols.*"]
            BasicLib["basic.*"]
            NumericLib["numeric.*"]
            UtilityLib["utility.*"]
            ExternalLib["external.*"]
        end
    end
    
    PyRosettaBuild["PyRosetta/build.py"] --> PyBindingGen["Python Binding Generation"]
    PyBindingGen --> PyRosettaModule["PyRosetta Module"]
    
    Libraries --> PyRosettaBuild
```

The build system:
- Uses `.src.settings` files to define which source files to compile
- Utilizes CMake to generate build files for different platforms
- Uses Ninja as the underlying build system for efficiency
- Organizes code into multiple libraries (core, protocols, etc.)
- Supports both compiled applications and Python bindings

Sources: [source/pilot_apps.src.settings.all](), [source/src/devel.src.settings]()

## Testing Framework

Rosetta includes a comprehensive testing framework to ensure correctness and prevent regressions.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Testing Types"
        UnitTests["Unit Tests"]
        IntegrationTests["Integration Tests"]
        ScientificTests["Scientific Tests"]
        RegressionTests["Regression Tests"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Test Infrastructure"
        TestRunner["Test Runner"]
        TestDatabase["Test Database"]
        TestInputs["Test Input Files"]
        TestScripts["Test Scripts"]
    end
    
    UnitTests --> TestRunner
    IntegrationTests --> TestRunner
    ScientificTests --> TestRunner
    RegressionTests --> TestRunner
    
    TestRunner --> TestResults["Test Results"]
    TestInputs --> UnitTests
    TestInputs --> IntegrationTests
    TestDatabase --> ScientificTests
    TestScripts --> TestRunner
```

The testing framework:
- Includes unit tests for individual components
- Provides integration tests for complex interactions between components
- Includes scientific tests that validate biological accuracy
- Uses regression tests to prevent functionality changes

Sources: [source/test/core.test.settings](), [source/test/protocols.test.settings]()

## Summary

The Rosetta software suite employs a modular, object-oriented architecture with several key components:

1. **Core Data Structures**: `Pose`, `Conformation`, `Residue`, and `ResidueType` form the foundation for representing molecular structures.

2. **Scoring System**: The `ScoreFunction`, `EnergyMethod`, and `Energies` classes evaluate the energy of molecular structures.

3. **Protocol System**: `Mover`s transform structures, `Filter`s evaluate them, and factories create these components.

4. **I/O System**: Handles reading and writing structures in various formats.

5. **Registration System**: Allows extension of functionality through component registration.

6. **Interfaces**: RosettaScripts (XML) and PyRosetta (Python) provide accessible interfaces to Rosetta functionality.

7. **Build System**: Manages compilation of components and creation of applications.

The architecture emphasizes modularity, extensibility, and reusability, allowing for easy addition of new functionality without modifying existing code.

Sources: [source/src/core/chemical/ResidueType.cc](), [source/src/core/pose/Pose.cc](), [source/src/core/conformation/Conformation.cc](), [source/src/core/scoring/ScoreTypeManager.cc](), [source/src/protocols/init/init.MoverRegistrators.ihh]()

## Purpose and Scope

This document describes the Rosetta build system, which is responsible for compiling the Rosetta codebase into executable programs and libraries. It explains the main components, configuration options, and process for building Rosetta from source code. The build system is based on CMake and Ninja, with Python scripts that orchestrate the build process.

For information about organizing code and creating new source files, see the [Architecture Overview](#1.1). For testing frameworks, see [Testing and Development](#6).

Sources: [source/ninja_build.py](), [source/cmake/build_util.py](), [source/cmake/make_project.py]()

## Build System Architecture

The Rosetta build system employs a multi-layer architecture to transform source code into executable programs and libraries. The system leverages CMake for configuration and Ninja for efficient parallel compilation.

### Key Components Diagram

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Build Entry Points"
        NinjaBuild["ninja_build.py"]
    end

    subgraph "Configuration"
        BuildSettings["build.settings\n*.src.settings"]
        MakeProject["make_project.py"]
        BuildUtil["build_util.py"]
    end

    subgraph "Generation Tools"
        CMake["CMake"]
        Ninja["Ninja"]
    end

    subgraph "Outputs"
        Executables["Executables"]
        Libraries["Libraries"]
    end

    NinjaBuild --> MakeProject
    NinjaBuild --> CMake
    NinjaBuild --> Ninja
    
    BuildSettings --> MakeProject
    BuildSettings --> CMake
    
    MakeProject --> CMake
    BuildUtil --> MakeProject
    
    CMake --> Ninja
    Ninja --> Executables
    Ninja --> Libraries
```

- **ninja_build.py**: The main entry point script that coordinates the build process
- **build.settings/src.settings files**: Define which source files to compile and how
- **make_project.py**: Processes source settings and generates project files
- **CMake**: Configures the build environment and generates Ninja build files
- **Ninja**: The build tool that actually compiles the code in parallel

Sources: [source/ninja_build.py](), [source/cmake/make_project.py:30-66]()

## Build Process Workflow

The build process involves several steps, as illustrated in the following diagram:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant NinjaBuild as "ninja_build.py"
    participant MakeProject as "make_project.py"
    participant Settings as "*.src.settings"
    participant CMake
    participant Ninja
    participant Compiler

    User->>NinjaBuild: Execute with options
    NinjaBuild->>MakeProject: Generate project files
    MakeProject->>Settings: Load source definitions
    Settings-->>MakeProject: Source files to compile
    MakeProject-->>NinjaBuild: CMake files generated
    NinjaBuild->>CMake: Configure build
    CMake->>Ninja: Generate build files
    NinjaBuild->>Ninja: Execute build
    Ninja->>Compiler: Compile source files
    Compiler-->>Ninja: Compiled object files
    Ninja->>Ninja: Link objects
    Ninja-->>NinjaBuild: Build complete
    NinjaBuild-->>User: Build results
```

1. User invokes `ninja_build.py` with desired build options
2. The script processes configuration and calls `make_project.py`
3. `make_project.py` processes the source settings files to determine what to build
4. CMake is invoked to configure the build environment and generate Ninja build files
5. Ninja compiles the source files and links them into executables and libraries
6. Results are returned to the user

Sources: [source/ninja_build.py:42-70](), [source/cmake/make_project.py:33-61]()

## Source Settings Files

The Rosetta build system uses `.src.settings` files to define which source files should be compiled. These files are Python scripts that define dictionaries of sources organized by directory.

### Structure and Format

Source settings files follow this general format:

```python
sources = {
    "directory_path": [
        "source_file1",
        "source_file2",
        # more source files
    ],
    # more directories
}
```

The `sources` dictionary maps directory paths to lists of source files. For example, in `protocols.3.src.settings`:

```python
sources = {
    "protocols/simple_pose_metric_calculators": [
        "BuriedUnsatisfiedPolarsCalculator",
        "NumberHBondsCalculator",
    ],
    "protocols/aa_composition": [
        "AddCompositionConstraintMover",
        "AddMHCEpitopeConstraintMover",
        # more files
    ],
    # more directories
}
```

Each project in Rosetta has its own `.src.settings` file that defines the sources for that project.

Sources: [source/src/protocols.3.src.settings:12-37](), [source/src/pilot_apps.src.settings.all:27-184]()

## Project Organization

Rosetta's codebase is organized into multiple projects, with dependencies between them:

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Applications"
        Apps["apps"]
        PilotApps["pilot_apps"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Core Libraries"
        Core["core.1-6"]
        Basic["basic"]
        Numeric["numeric"]
        Utility["utility"]
        ObjexxFCL["ObjexxFCL"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Protocol Libraries"
        Protocols["protocols.1-8"] 
        ProtocolsA["protocols_a.1-5"]
        ProtocolsB["protocols_b.1-5"]
        ProtocolsC["protocols_c.1-5"]
        Devel["devel"]
    end
    
    Apps --> Protocols
    PilotApps --> Protocols
    
    Protocols --> Core
    ProtocolsA --> Core
    ProtocolsB --> Core
    ProtocolsC --> Core
    
    Core --> Basic
    Core --> Numeric
    Core --> Utility
    Basic --> ObjexxFCL
    Numeric --> ObjexxFCL
    Utility --> ObjexxFCL
    
    Devel --> Protocols
```

Each project is defined by its own `.src.settings` file and is compiled into a separate library or set of executables. The subprojects list in the settings files defines the dependencies between projects.

Sources: [source/src/pilot_apps.src.settings.all:1190-1226](), [source/test/protocols.test.settings:890-924]()

## Build Configuration Options

The build system supports various configuration options that control how Rosetta is built:

### Compilers

Rosetta supports multiple compilers, including:
- GCC
- Clang
- ICC (Intel Compiler)
- MSVC (Microsoft Visual C++)

### Build Modes

Different build modes optimize for different purposes:

| Build Mode | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| debug | Includes debugging symbols, minimal optimization |
| release | Optimized for performance, no debugging symbols |
| release_debug | Performance optimizations with debugging symbols |
| release_symbols | Like release, but with debugging symbols |
| profile | Includes profiling information |
| addsan | Address sanitizer for memory error detection |
| tsan | Thread sanitizer for detecting thread safety issues |
| ubsan | Undefined behavior sanitizer |

### Platform Options

The build system supports multiple platforms:
- Linux
- macOS
- Windows (including Cygwin)

### Additional Options

Extra configuration options include:
- cxx14/cxx17/cxx20: C++ standard to use
- mpi: Enable Message Passing Interface for parallelization
- static: Build using static linking
- python: Link to Python interpreter
- openmp: Enable OpenMP for parallel processing
- tensorflow/tensorflow_gpu: Build with TensorFlow support

Sources: [source/tools/build/options.settings:9-210](), [source/tools/build/basic.settings:58-686]()

## Build Commands

### Basic Build Commands

To build Rosetta with default settings:

```bash
./ninja_build.py
```

### Building with Specific Options

To build with a specific compiler and build mode:

```bash
./ninja_build.py --compiler clang --mode release
```

### Building Specific Targets

To build only certain applications:

```bash
./ninja_build.py --target AbinitioRelax score_jd2
```

### Cleaning the Build Directory

To clean the build directory before building:

```bash
./ninja_build.py --clean
```

### Getting Help

To see all available options:

```bash
./ninja_build.py --help
```

Sources: [source/ninja_build.py:44-95](), [source/ninja_build.py:151-226]()

## Component Registration System

Rosetta uses a registration system to make components discoverable at runtime. This is handled during the build process:

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Registration Files"
        MoverReg["MoverRegistrators.ihh"]
        FilterReg["FilterRegistrators.ihh"]
        TaskOpReg["TaskOperationRegistrators.ihh"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Creator Files"
        MoverCreator["MoverCreators.ihh"]
        FilterCreator["FilterCreators.ihh"]
        TaskOpCreator["TaskOperationCreators.ihh"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Factory System"
        MoverFactory["MoverFactory"]
        FilterFactory["FilterFactory"]
        TaskOpFactory["TaskOperationFactory"]
    end
    
    MoverReg --> MoverFactory
    FilterReg --> FilterFactory
    TaskOpReg --> TaskOpFactory
    
    MoverCreator --> MoverReg
    FilterCreator --> FilterReg
    TaskOpCreator --> TaskOpReg
```

During compilation, registrator objects are instantiated as static objects. When the program starts, these objects register their corresponding creator classes with the appropriate factories, making components available through the factory system.

Sources: [source/src/protocols/init/init.MoverRegistrators.ihh:19-41](), [source/src/protocols/init/init.MoverCreators.ihh:15-61](), [source/src/protocols/init/init.FilterRegistrators.ihh:17-80]()

## Versioning and Updating

The build system includes scripts for updating version information and other dependencies:

- `update_version.py`: Updates version information
- `update_options.sh`: Updates build options
- `update_submodules.sh`: Updates Git submodules
- `update_ResidueType_enum_files.sh`: Updates residue type enumeration files

These scripts are automatically called as needed during the build process.

Sources: [source/cmake/make_project.py:17-30]()

## Common Build Issues

### Missing Dependencies

If external dependencies are missing, the build will fail. Ensure all required libraries are installed.

### Compiler Version Compatibility

Different compilers and versions may have different behaviors. The build system supports specific compiler versions listed in the options settings.

### Build Performance

For faster builds:
- Use the Ninja build system (default)
- Enable parallel builds with multiple cores
- Build only the targets you need
- Use ccache if available

Sources: [source/tools/build/options.settings:11-17](), [source/ninja_build.py:151-175]()

## Summary

The Rosetta build system provides a flexible, platform-independent way to compile the Rosetta codebase. It leverages CMake and Ninja for configuration and compilation, with Python scripts that orchestrate the build process. The system supports multiple compilers, build modes, and platforms, allowing users to tailor the build to their specific needs.

This page describes the foundational data structures used throughout the Rosetta molecular modeling suite. These structures represent biomolecular systems and their components, from individual atoms to complete macromolecules. Understanding these core structures is essential for working with Rosetta, as they form the basis for all simulations, analyses, and manipulations of molecular structures.

For information about the scoring system that evaluates these structures, see [Scoring System](#3). For details on protocols that manipulate these structures, see [Protocol System](#4).

## Hierarchical Organization

Rosetta's core data structures follow a hierarchical organization, where smaller components are combined to create more complex structures. At the highest level is the `Pose`, which represents an entire molecular structure. A `Pose` contains a `Conformation`, which in turn is composed of `Residue` objects. Each `Residue` references a specific `ResidueType` that defines its chemical identity.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Core Class Hierarchy"
        Pose["Pose"]
        Conf["Conformation"]
        Res["Residue"]
        ResType["ResidueType"]
        Atom["Atom"]
        FoldTree["FoldTree"]
        AtomTree["AtomTree"]
        PDBInfo["PDBInfo"]
        Energies["Energies"]
        
        Pose --> Conf
        Pose --> Energies
        Pose --> PDBInfo
        Conf --> Res
        Conf --> FoldTree
        Conf --> AtomTree
        Res --> ResType
        Res --> Atom
    end
```

Sources: [source/src/core/pose/Pose.hh:135-147](), [source/src/core/conformation/Conformation.hh:91-125](), [source/src/core/conformation/Residue.hh:84-133](), [source/src/core/chemical/ResidueType.hh:96-124]()

## ResidueType

`ResidueType` defines the chemical properties of a residue (e.g., amino acid, nucleotide, ligand) without specifying its spatial coordinates in a particular molecular context. It serves as a template from which individual `Residue` instances are created.

### Key Properties

- **Atoms**: Defines the composition, atom types, and ideal geometry
- **Bonds**: Specifies connectivity between atoms
- **Torsion Angles**: Defines rotatable bonds (chi angles)
- **Connectivity**: Defines how residues can connect to others (e.g., peptide bonds)
- **Properties**: Indicates characteristics like polarity, charge, aromaticity

### Chemical Information

`ResidueType` maintains references to several important data structures:

- **AtomType**: Defines chemical properties of atoms
- **Element**: Specifies the chemical element of each atom
- **MMAtomType**: For molecular mechanics force field typing
- **Atomic Charges**: Both formal and partial charges
- **Orbital Information**: For specialized calculations involving electrons

```mermaid
graph TD
    ResidueType["ResidueType"]
    AtomType["AtomType"]
    Element["Element"]
    MMAtomType["MMAtomType"]
    Bond["Bond"]
    ResidueProperty["ResidueProperty"]
    ResidueConnection["ResidueConnection"]
    ChiDefinition["Chi Angle Definition"]
    
    ResidueType --> AtomType
    ResidueType --> Element
    ResidueType --> MMAtomType
    ResidueType --> Bond
    ResidueType --> ResidueProperty
    ResidueType --> ResidueConnection
    ResidueType --> ChiDefinition
    
    ResidueProperty -->|examples| Properties["PROTEIN, RNA, DNA,\nLIGAND, POLYMER, etc."]
```

Sources: [source/src/core/chemical/ResidueType.hh:124-177](), [source/src/core/chemical/ResidueType.cc:90-177]()

### Creation and Immutability

`ResidueType` is immutable once created. It is typically loaded from a params file using the `MutableResidueType` intermediate class:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    ParamsFile["Params File"] --> MutableResidueType["MutableResidueType"]
    MutableResidueType -->|"make()"| ResidueType["ResidueType (immutable)"]
```

Sources: [source/src/core/chemical/ResidueType.cc:96-126](), [source/src/core/chemical/residue_io.cc:80-200]()

## Residue

`Residue` represents an instance of a `ResidueType` positioned in 3D space. It combines the chemical definition from `ResidueType` with specific spatial coordinates. It also stores instance-specific information such as sequence position and chain ID.

### Key Properties

- **Coordinates**: 3D positions of all atoms
- **Torsion Angles**: Current values of phi, psi, omega, and chi angles
- **Sequence Information**: Position and chain ID
- **Residue Connections**: Actual connections to other residues

```mermaid
graph TD
    Residue["Residue"]
    ResidueType["ResidueType"]
    Atoms["Atoms (with coordinates)"]
    ChiAngles["Chi Angles"]
    MainchainTorsions["Mainchain Torsions"]
    ConnectMap["Connect Map"]
    
    Residue --> ResidueType
    Residue --> Atoms
    Residue --> ChiAngles
    Residue --> MainchainTorsions
    Residue --> ConnectMap
```

Sources: [source/src/core/conformation/Residue.hh:84-120](), [source/src/core/conformation/Residue.cc:92-149]()

### Creation and Modification

Residues can be created directly from a `ResidueType` or by copying another `Residue`. When creating a rotamer (alternative side-chain conformation), a new `Residue` is created with the same backbone but different chi angles:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    ResidueType["ResidueType"] -->|"new Residue()"| Residue["New Residue\n(ideal coords)"]
    ExistingResidue["Existing Residue"] -->|"Residue constructor"| Rotamer["New Rotamer\n(same backbone,\ndifferent side chain)"]
```

Sources: [source/src/core/conformation/Residue.cc:92-246]()

## Conformation

`Conformation` is a container for a collection of `Residue` objects that form a complete molecular structure. It manages residue-residue relationships and handles the kinematics (how movement of one part affects others) through the `FoldTree` and `AtomTree` classes.

### Key Properties

- **Residue Collection**: Container of all residues
- **FoldTree**: Defines kinematic connectivity
- **AtomTree**: Implements coordinate calculations
- **Chain Information**: Manages chain breaks and IDs

```mermaid
graph TD
    Conformation["Conformation"]
    Residues["Residues[]"]
    FoldTree["FoldTree"]
    AtomTree["AtomTree"]
    ChainEndings["Chain Endings"]
    ResidueTypeSet["ResidueTypeSet"]
    
    Conformation --> Residues
    Conformation --> FoldTree
    Conformation --> AtomTree
    Conformation --> ChainEndings
    Conformation --> ResidueTypeSet
    
    FoldTree --> Edges["Edges (PEPTIDE/JUMP/CHEMICAL)"]
    AtomTree --> CoordinateUpdates["Coordinate Updates"]
```

Sources: [source/src/core/conformation/Conformation.hh:91-125](), [source/src/core/conformation/Conformation.cc:109-196]()

### Kinematic Control with FoldTree

The `FoldTree` defines how movements propagate through the structure. It consists of edges that can be:

- **PEPTIDE**: Standard peptide bond connection
- **JUMP**: Connection between non-bonded residues (e.g., between chains)
- **CHEMICAL**: Non-standard chemical connection (e.g., disulfide bonds)

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "FoldTree Example"
        direction LR
        Root[("Root Residue")]
        Chain1["Chain 1"]
        Chain2["Chain 2"]
        Ligand["Ligand"]
        
        Root -->|"JUMP 1"| Chain1
        Root -->|"JUMP 2"| Chain2
        Chain2 -->|"JUMP 3"| Ligand
        
        subgraph "Chain 1 Residues"
            R1_1["Residue 1"] --- R1_2["Residue 2"] --- R1_3["Residue 3"]
        end
        
        subgraph "Chain 2 Residues"
            R2_1["Residue 4"] --- R2_2["Residue 5"] --- R2_3["Residue 6"]
        end
    end
```

Sources: [source/src/core/conformation/Conformation.cc:813-847](), [source/src/core/pose/util.cc:153-315]()

## Pose

`Pose` is the top-level container that represents a complete molecular structure. It combines a `Conformation` with scoring information (`Energies`), constraints, and data needed for mapping to PDB files (`PDBInfo`).

### Key Components

- **Conformation**: Contains residues and kinematics
- **Energies**: Stores energy terms and values
- **PDBInfo**: Maps to PDB file information
- **Constraints**: Restraints applied during scoring/modeling
- **Data Cache**: Additional data associated with the pose

```mermaid
graph TD
    Pose["Pose"]
    Conformation["Conformation"]
    Energies["Energies"]
    PDBInfo["PDBInfo"]
    ConstraintSet["ConstraintSet"]
    DataCache["DataCache"]
    Metrics["PoseMetricContainer"]
    
    Pose --> Conformation
    Pose --> Energies
    Pose --> PDBInfo
    Pose --> ConstraintSet
    Pose --> DataCache
    Pose --> Metrics
    
    Energies --> EnergyTerms["Energy Terms\n(score components)"]
    ConstraintSet --> Constraints["Constraints\n(restraints)"]
    PDBInfo --> ChainInfo["Chain IDs & Numbering"]
    PDBInfo --> Remarks["PDB Remarks"]
    DataCache --> CacheableData["Cacheable Data\n(auxiliary information)"]
```

Sources: [source/src/core/pose/Pose.hh:125-150](), [source/src/core/pose/Pose.cc:108-142]()

### Creation and Manipulation

Poses are typically created by reading external files (PDB, mmCIF) using a conversion pipeline:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    PDBFile["PDB/mmCIF File"] --> StructFileRep["StructFileRep"]
    StructFileRep -->|"PoseFromSFRBuilder"| Pose["Pose"]
    
    Pose -->|"Protocols/Movers"| ModifiedPose["Modified Pose"]
    ModifiedPose -->|"ScoreFunction"| ScoredPose["Scored Pose"]
    ScoredPose -->|"Output"| OutputFiles["Output Files\n(PDB, mmCIF, silent)"]
```

Sources: [source/src/core/io/pose_from_sfr/PoseFromSFRBuilder.cc:115-140](), [source/src/core/pose/Pose.cc:169-195]()

## Key Support Classes

### FoldTree

`FoldTree` defines the kinematic connectivity of residues in a molecular structure. It's a directed graph where:

- Nodes represent residues
- Edges represent connections between residues
- Edge types can be PEPTIDE, JUMP, or CHEMICAL
- A root node is defined as the reference point

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "FoldTree Components"
        Edge["Edge"]
        EdgeTypes["Edge Types"]
        Root["Root Node"]
        
        Edge --> EdgeTypes
        Edge --> StartRes["Start Residue"]
        Edge --> EndRes["End Residue"]
        
        EdgeTypes -->|types| Types["PEPTIDE\nJUMP\nCHEMICAL"]
    end
```

Sources: [source/src/core/pose/util.cc:152-315](), [source/src/core/conformation/Conformation.cc:813-833]()

### AtomTree

`AtomTree` implements the actual coordinate calculations based on the `FoldTree`. It:

- Tracks atom coordinates
- Updates coordinates when torsion angles change
- Propagates changes according to the FoldTree

Sources: [source/src/core/conformation/Conformation.cc:126-137](), [source/src/core/conformation/Conformation.hh:744-780]()

## Data Flow Between Core Structures

This diagram illustrates how information flows between core data structures during typical operations:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Initialization"
        PDBFile["PDB File"] --> StructFileRep
        StructFileRep -->|"build_pose()"| Pose
        ResidueTypeSet -->|"provides templates"| Pose
    end
    
    subgraph "Structural Modification"
        Pose -->|"set_chi()"| Residue
        Residue -->|"updates"| Atom
        Residue -->|"notifies"| Conformation
        Conformation -->|"updates"| AtomTree
        FoldTree -->|"defines propagation"| AtomTree
    end
    
    subgraph "Scoring"
        Pose -->|"score()"| ScoreFunction
        ScoreFunction -->|"populates"| Energies
        Pose -->|"stores"| Energies
    end
    
    subgraph "Output"
        Pose -->|"dump_pdb()"| OutputPDB["Output PDB"]
    end
```

Sources: [source/src/core/io/pose_from_sfr/PoseFromSFRBuilder.cc:115-140](), [source/src/core/pose/Pose.cc:325-425]()

## Common Operations

Below are some common operations that utilize the core data structures:

### Creating a Pose from a PDB file

```
core::pose::Pose pose;
core::import_pose::pose_from_file(pose, "input.pdb");
```

### Retrieving Atom Coordinates

```
// Get atom coordinates from a Pose
core::Vector const & xyz = pose.residue(residue_index).atom(atom_index).xyz();

// Get coordinates via an AtomID
core::id::AtomID atom_id(atom_index, residue_index);
core::Vector const & xyz = pose.xyz(atom_id);
```

### Modifying Torsion Angles

```
// Set a chi angle
pose.set_chi(chi_index, residue_index, new_angle_degrees);

// Set phi/psi
pose.set_phi(residue_index, new_phi_degrees);
pose.set_psi(residue_index, new_psi_degrees);
```

### Adding a Residue

```
// Append residue via peptide bond
core::conformation::ResidueOP new_residue = core::conformation::ResidueFactory::create_residue(residue_type);
pose.append_residue_by_bond(*new_residue);

// Add residue by jump (non-bonded)
pose.append_residue_by_jump(*new_residue, anchor_residue);
```

Sources: [source/src/core/pose/util.cc:315-440](), [source/src/core/pose/Pose.cc:652-750]()

## Related Systems

The core data structures described here are used by many other systems in Rosetta:

- **Scoring System**: Evaluates energies based on these structures
- **Protocol System**: Modifies these structures to perform modeling tasks
- **I/O System**: Reads/writes these structures from/to external files
- **Symmetry System**: Extends these structures to handle molecular symmetry

For more information on these systems, refer to their respective wiki pages.

This document explains the Pose and Conformation system, which forms the core data representation in the Rosetta molecular modeling suite. Understanding these components is essential for working with Rosetta's codebase and developing new protocols within the framework. For information about the Residue and ResidueType components that work closely with Pose and Conformation, see [Residue and ResidueType](#2.2).

## System Overview

The Pose and Conformation system provides a hierarchical data structure representing molecular structures with their 3D coordinates, chemical properties, connectivity, and energetics. This hierarchy forms the backbone of all structural manipulation and energy calculations in Rosetta.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Pose {
        -Conformation conformation_
        -Energies energies_
        -PDBInfo pdb_info_
        -DataCache data_
        +size() Size
        +residue(Size) Residue&
        +energies() Energies&
        +set_dof(TorsionID, Real)
    }
    
    class Conformation {
        -vector~ResidueOP~ residues_
        -FoldTree fold_tree_
        -AtomTree atom_tree_
        -ParametersSet parameters_set_
        +size() Size
        +residue(Size) Residue&
        +update_residue_neighbors()
    }
    
    class Residue {
        -ResidueType& rsd_type_
        -vector~Atom~ atoms_
        -vector~Real~ chi_
        -vector~Real~ mainchain_torsions_
        +natoms() Size
        +atom(Size) Atom&
        +chi(Size) Real
    }
    
    class ResidueType {
        -vector~string~ atom_names_
        -vector~AtomType~ atom_types_
        -vector~AtomIndices~ bonded_neighbor_
        -vector~AtomICoor~ icoor_
        +natoms() Size
        +nchi() Size
        +atom_name(Size) string
    }
    
    Pose *-- Conformation : contains
    Conformation *-- Residue : contains many
    Residue --> ResidueType : references
```

Sources:
- [source/src/core/pose/Pose.hh]()
- [source/src/core/conformation/Conformation.hh]()
- [source/src/core/conformation/Residue.hh]()
- [source/src/core/chemical/ResidueType.hh]()

## The Pose Object

The Pose is the central data structure representing a complete molecular model in Rosetta. It's the primary object that protocols (usually implemented as Movers) manipulate.

### Core Components

A Pose contains several key components:

1. **Conformation** (`conformation_`): Manages 3D coordinates and molecular connectivity
2. **Energies** (`energies_`): Stores energy calculations for the structure 
3. **PDBInfo** (`pdb_info_`): Contains PDB-specific information like chain IDs and numbering
4. **DataCache** (`data_`): Stores additional data associated with the pose

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Pose Components"
        A["Pose"] --- B["Conformation\n(3D structure)"]
        A --- C["Energies\n(energy calculations)"]
        A --- D["PDBInfo\n(metadata)"]
        A --- E["DataCache\n(auxiliary data)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "External Interactions"
        F["ScoreFunction"] --> A
        G["Mover"] --> A
        H["Filter"] --> A
    end
```

Sources:
- [source/src/core/pose/Pose.cc:108-127]() - Default initialization function
- [source/src/core/pose/Pose.cc:130-193]() - Copy constructor

### Primary Functionality

The Pose class provides methods for:

- Accessing residues: `residue(Size)` returns a particular residue
- Managing energies: `energies()` accesses the energy calculations
- Setting degrees of freedom: `set_dof(TorsionID, value)` changes torsion angles
- Handling constraints: `add_constraint(Constraint)` adds constraints
- Structural manipulation: Internally manages coordinate updates

## The Conformation Object

The Conformation class is contained within a Pose and manages the 3D structure of the molecular model. It's responsible for the geometric representation and coordinates of all atoms.

### Core Components

A Conformation contains:

1. **Residues** (`residues_`): A vector of Residue objects that make up the molecule
2. **FoldTree** (`fold_tree_`): Defines the kinematic connectivity between residues
3. **AtomTree** (`atom_tree_`): Manages atom-level connectivity and coordinate updates
4. **Chain information** (`chain_endings_`): Records where protein chains begin and end
5. **Secondary structure** (`secstruct_`): Records secondary structure assignments

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Conformation Structure"
        A["Conformation"] --- B["Residues"]
        A --- C["FoldTree\n(kinematic connectivity)"]
        A --- D["AtomTree\n(atom connectivity)"]
        A --- E["Chain information"]
        A --- F["Secondary structure"]
    end
    
    B --- G["Residue 1"]
    B --- H["Residue 2"]
    B --- I["Residue n"]
```

Sources:
- [source/src/core/conformation/Conformation.cc:116-127]() - Default constructor
- [source/src/core/conformation/Conformation.cc:130-193]() - Copy constructor
- [source/src/core/conformation/Conformation.hh:116-193]() - Class definition

### Primary Functionality

The Conformation class provides methods for:

- Accessing residues: `residue(Size)` returns a reference to a residue
- Managing the fold tree: `fold_tree()` accesses the kinematic connectivity
- Updating coordinates: `update_residue_coordinates()` updates atom positions
- Handling connectivity: `connect_residues()` creates chemical bonds between residues
- Detecting clashes: `detect_self_clash()` checks for atomic overlaps

## Coordinate Update Mechanism

When a degree of freedom (DOF) in a Pose is modified, a cascade of coordinate updates occurs:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Pose
    participant Conformation
    participant Residue
    participant AtomTree
    
    Pose->>Conformation: set_torsion(torsion_id, value)
    Conformation->>Residue: set_chi(chi_num, value)
    Residue-->>Conformation: residue_coordinates_need_updating = true
    Conformation->>AtomTree: marks affected DOFs
    AtomTree-->>Conformation: updates AtomTree coordinates
    Conformation->>Residue: update atom coordinates
    Residue-->>Pose: coordinates updated
    Pose->>Pose: notify observers
```

Sources:
- [source/src/core/pose/util.cc:93-127]() - Torsion setting functionality
- [source/src/core/conformation/Conformation.cc:200-300]() - Coordinate update methods

## Key Operations

The Pose and Conformation system enables several crucial operations for molecular modeling:

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["Create Pose"] --> B["Modify Structure"]
    B --> C["Score Pose"]
    B --> D["Apply Protocol"]
    D --> C
    C --> E["Accept/Reject Changes"]
    E --> B
```

### Common Operations

1. **Creating a Pose**: 
   - From a PDB file using `core::import_pose::pose_from_file()`
   - Programmatically building a Pose residue by residue

2. **Modifying a Pose**:
   - Setting torsion angles: `pose.set_phi()`, `pose.set_psi()`, `pose.set_chi()`
   - Replacing residues: `pose.replace_residue()`
   - Connecting residues: `core::pose::add_variant_type_to_pose_residue()`

3. **Scoring a Pose**:
   - Applying a ScoreFunction: `scorefxn(pose)`
   - Accessing energies: `pose.energies().total_energy()`

4. **Applying Protocols**:
   - Using Movers to make complex changes: `mover.apply(pose)`
   - Common movers include `FastRelax`, `PackRotamersMover`, and `MinMover`

Sources:
- [source/src/core/pose/util.cc]() - Pose utility functions
- [source/src/protocols/init/init.MoverRegistrators.ihh]() - Available Movers
- [source/src/protocols/init/init.FilterRegistrators.ihh]() - Available Filters

## Relationship to Other Systems

The Pose and Conformation system interacts with several other key systems in Rosetta:

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["Pose & Conformation"] --> B["Scoring System"]
    A --> C["Protocol System"]
    A --> D["I/O System"]
    A --> E["Build/Script System"]
    
    B --> F["ScoreFunction"]
    B --> G["EnergyMethod"]
    
    C --> H["Mover"]
    C --> I["Filter"]
    
    D --> J["PDB I/O"]
    D --> K["Silent File I/O"]
    
    E --> L["RosettaScripts"]
    E --> M["PyRosetta"]
```

Sources:
- [source/src/protocols/init/init.MoverCreators.ihh]() - Integration with protocols system
- [source/src/protocols/init/init.FilterCreators.ihh]() - Integration with filters system

## Conclusion

The Pose and Conformation system serves as the foundation for molecular representation in Rosetta. The Pose provides a high-level interface for structural manipulation and energy calculations, while the Conformation manages the geometric representation and coordinates. Together, they enable the powerful molecular modeling capabilities that Rosetta is known for.

Sources:
- [source/src/core/pose/Pose.cc]() 
- [source/src/core/conformation/Conformation.cc]()
- [source/src/core/conformation/Residue.cc]()

This page documents the `Residue` and `ResidueType` classes in Rosetta, which serve as the fundamental data structures for representing molecular components. Together, they form a type-instance relationship where `ResidueType` defines the chemical template and `Residue` represents a specific instance with position-specific data. For information about the higher-level containers that work with residues, see [Pose and Conformation](#2.1).

## Overview

The Residue-ResidueType relationship follows a type-instance pattern:

- **ResidueType**: A constant, immutable template that defines the chemical properties, ideal geometry, and connectivity of a particular molecular component (like an amino acid, nucleotide, carbohydrate, or ligand).
- **Residue**: A specific instance of a ResidueType with unique coordinates, sequence position, and conformation.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class ResidueType {
        +natoms() Size
        +nheavyatoms() Size
        +atom_name(Size) string
        +atom_index(string) Size
        +atom_type(Size) AtomType
        +ideal_xyz(Size) Vector
        +is_polymer() bool
        +is_protein() bool
        +is_dna() bool
        +ResidueType(MutableResidueType)
    }
    
    class Residue {
        -ResidueTypeCOP rsd_type_ptr_
        -vector~Atom~ atoms_
        -Size seqpos_
        -int chain_
        -vector~Real~ chi_
        -vector~Real~ mainchain_torsions_
        +xyz(Size) Vector
        +set_xyz(Size, Vector) void
        +atom(Size) Atom
        +name3() string
        +type() ResidueType
        +chi(Size) Real
        +Residue(ResidueTypeCOP)
    }
    
    class Atom {
        -Vector xyz_
        -Size type_index_
        -Size mm_type_index_
        +xyz() Vector
        +set_xyz(Vector) void
    }
    
    Residue --o ResidueType : references
    Residue --* Atom : contains
```

Sources: [source/src/core/chemical/ResidueType.hh:95-124](source/src/core/chemical/ResidueType.hh:95-124), [source/src/core/conformation/Residue.hh:63-85](source/src/core/conformation/Residue.hh:63-85)

## ResidueType

A `ResidueType` defines the chemical identity and properties of a molecular component. These objects are immutable once created and contain all the information needed to create specific instances of residues.

### Creation and Origin

ResidueTypes are created in two primary ways:

1. **From parameter files**: Most ResidueTypes are generated from parameter files (`.params`) stored in the Rosetta database.
2. **From MutableResidueType**: ResidueTypes are constructed from MutableResidueType objects, which are modifiable versions used during initialization and patching.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    ParamsFile["Params File"] --> MutableResidueType
    Patch["Patch Operations"] --> MutableResidueType
    MutableResidueType --> ResidueType["ResidueType (immutable)"]
    ResidueType --> ResidueTypeSet
    ResidueTypeSet --> Residue
```

Sources: [source/src/core/chemical/ResidueType.cc:100-113](source/src/core/chemical/ResidueType.cc:100-113), [source/src/core/chemical/residue_io.cc](source/src/core/chemical/residue_io.cc)

### Atom Representation

ResidueType stores atom information in a well-defined order to optimize performance and facilitate look-up operations:

1. Heavy backbone atoms
2. Heavy sidechain atoms
3. Backbone hydrogens
4. Sidechain hydrogens

```
AtomInfo storage order:
1-N_backbone_heavyatoms_: Heavy backbone atoms
N_backbone_heavyatoms_+1 to nheavyatoms_: Heavy sidechain atoms
nheavyatoms_+1 to first_sidechain_hydrogen_-1: Backbone hydrogens
first_sidechain_hydrogen_ to natoms_: Sidechain hydrogens
```

Each atom is identified by:
- Name (e.g., "CA", "N", "O")
- Index (numerical position in the atom array)
- Type (pointer to an AtomType object)
- Properties (element, charge, connectivity)

Methods for atom access:
- `atom_name(Size index)`: Get atom name by index
- `atom_index(string name)`: Get index by atom name
- `natoms()`: Get total number of atoms
- `nheavyatoms()`: Get number of heavy atoms (non-hydrogen)

Sources: [source/src/core/chemical/ResidueType.hh:384-422](source/src/core/chemical/ResidueType.hh:384-422), [source/src/core/chemical/ResidueType.cc:1099-1132](source/src/core/chemical/ResidueType.cc:1099-1132)

### Bond Representation

ResidueType stores bond information to define the connectivity between atoms:

- Bonds between atoms
- Bond types (single, double, triple, etc.)
- Path distances between atoms (number of bonds that separate them)

Methods for bond access:
- `bonded_neighbor(Size atom_index)`: Get indices of atoms bonded to a given atom
- `atoms_are_bonded(Size atom1, Size atom2)`: Check if two atoms are bonded
- `bond_type(Size atom1, Size atom2)`: Get the type of bond between two atoms
- `path_distance(Size atom1, Size atom2)`: Get the number of bonds in the shortest path between atoms

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A1["Atom 1 (idx=1)"] --- B1["Bond (single)"] --- A2["Atom 2 (idx=2)"]
    A2 --- B2["Bond (single)"] --- A3["Atom 3 (idx=3)"]
    A3 --- B3["Bond (double)"] --- A4["Atom 4 (idx=4)"]
    A2 --- B4["Bond (single)"] --- A5["Atom 5 (idx=5)"]
    
    subgraph "Path Distance Example"
        P1["path_distance(1,4) = 3"] 
        P2["path_distance(2,5) = 1"]
        P3["path_distance(1,5) = 2"]
    end
```

Sources: [source/src/core/chemical/ResidueType.hh:584-633](source/src/core/chemical/ResidueType.hh:584-633), [source/src/core/chemical/ResidueType.cc:243-293](source/src/core/chemical/ResidueType.cc:243-293)

### Properties

ResidueTypes have various properties that characterize their chemical and physical nature. These properties are defined in the parameter files and are used throughout Rosetta to determine how residues should be treated.

Common properties include:
- `POLYMER`: Indicates the residue can form polymer chains
- `PROTEIN`, `DNA`, `RNA`, `CARBOHYDRATE`: Indicates the molecule type
- `CHARGED`, `POLAR`, `AROMATIC`: Describes chemical characteristics
- `CANONICAL_AA`, `CANONICAL_NUCLEIC`: Indicates if it's a standard building block

Methods to check properties:
- `is_protein()`: Is this a protein residue?
- `is_dna()`: Is this a DNA residue?
- `is_polymer()`: Can this residue form polymer chains?
- `is_charged()`: Does this residue have a net charge?

Sources: [source/src/core/chemical/ResidueType.hh:556-773](source/src/core/chemical/ResidueType.hh:556-773), [source/src/core/chemical/residue_properties/general_properties.list:17-200](source/src/core/chemical/residue_properties/general_properties.list:17-200)

### Connections

ResidueTypes define connection points that determine how residues can link to one another. These are especially important for polymers and branched structures.

Types of connections:
- **Polymeric connections**: Lower and upper connecting atoms for forming polymer chains
- **Non-polymeric connections**: Branch points for tree-like structures

Methods for connections:
- `lower_connect()`: Get the lower polymer connection (e.g., N-terminus in proteins)
- `upper_connect()`: Get the upper polymer connection (e.g., C-terminus in proteins)
- `branch_connect_atoms()`: Get atoms that can form branch connections

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Protein Residue"
        N["N (lower_connect)"] --- CA["CA"] --- C["C (upper_connect)"]
        CA --- CB["CB"]
    end

    subgraph "Carbohydrate Residue"
        C1["C1 (upper_connect)"] --- C2["C2"] --- C3["C3"]
        C4["C4"] --- C5["C5"]
        C3 --- C4
        C3 --- Branch["O3 (branch_connect)"]
    end
```

Sources: [source/src/core/chemical/ResidueType.hh:426-539](source/src/core/chemical/ResidueType.hh:426-539), [source/src/core/chemical/ResidueType.cc:428-539](source/src/core/chemical/ResidueType.cc:428-539)

## Residue

A `Residue` represents a specific instance of a `ResidueType` with unique coordinates, sequence position, and conformation. Residues are the building blocks used to construct molecular models in Rosetta.

### Creation and Structure

Residues are created in several ways:

1. **From a ResidueType**: Basic instantiation with ideal geometry
2. **From another Residue**: Copy construction or template-based creation (e.g., for rotamers)
3. **From input files**: PDB files, silent files, etc.

Basic structure of a Residue:
- Reference to its ResidueType
- Vector of Atom objects (with coordinates)
- Sequence position and chain ID
- Torsion angles (chi, mainchain, etc.)
- Connection maps to other residues

```cpp
// Typical creation of a Residue
ResidueTypeCOP my_restype = chemical_manager->residue_type_set()->name_map("ALA");
ResidueOP my_residue = conformation::ResidueFactory::create_residue(*my_restype);
```

Sources: [source/src/core/conformation/Residue.cc:92-118](source/src/core/conformation/Residue.cc:92-118), [source/src/core/conformation/Residue.cc:162-206](source/src/core/conformation/Residue.cc:162-206)

### Atom Access and Manipulation

Unlike ResidueType, which provides information about ideal atom positions, Residue stores the actual coordinates of atoms in a specific molecular model.

Methods for atom access:
- `xyz(Size atom_index)`: Get coordinates of an atom by index
- `set_xyz(Size atom_index, Vector coords)`: Set coordinates of an atom
- `atom(Size atom_index)`: Get an Atom object by index
- `atom(string atom_name)`: Get an Atom object by name

```cpp
// Example operations
Vector ca_coords = residue.xyz(residue.atom_index("CA"));  // Get CA coordinates
residue.set_xyz(residue.atom_index("CA"), new_coords);     // Move CA atom
```

Sources: [source/src/core/conformation/Residue.hh:772-829](source/src/core/conformation/Residue.hh:772-829)

### Torsion Angles

Residues store and manipulate torsion angles that define their conformation. These include backbone torsions (phi, psi), sidechain torsions (chi angles), and ring torsions for cyclic structures.

Types of torsion angles:
- **Backbone torsions**: Define the protein backbone conformation
- **Chi angles**: Define the sidechain conformation
- **Nu angles**: Define internal ring conformations

Methods for torsion angles:
- `chi(Size chi_index)`: Get a chi angle value
- `set_chi(Size chi_index, Real value)`: Set a chi angle value
- `mainchain_torsion(Size index)`: Get a backbone torsion angle
- `update_chi_atoms()`: Update atom positions based on chi angles

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Torsion Angles"
        direction TB
        
        subgraph "Backbone"
            Phi["Phi (N-CA-C-N)"]
            Psi["Psi (CA-C-N-CA)"]
            Omega["Omega (C-N-CA-C)"]
        end
        
        subgraph "Sidechain"
            Chi1["Chi1 (N-CA-CB-CG)"]
            Chi2["Chi2 (CA-CB-CG-CD)"]
            Chi3["Chi3 (if present)"]
        end
        
        subgraph "Ring (e.g., Proline)"
            Nu1["Nu1"]
            Nu2["Nu2"]
            Nu3["Nu3"]
        end
    end
```

Sources: [source/src/core/conformation/Residue.hh:931-1000](source/src/core/conformation/Residue.hh:931-1000)

### Residue Connections

Residues maintain connection information that describes how they're linked to other residues in a model. These connections are essential for building complex molecular structures.

Types of connections:
- **Polymeric connections**: Connect residues in a linear chain (protein backbone, DNA backbone)
- **Non-polymeric connections**: Connect residues in branched structures (glycans, modified amino acids)
- **Pseudo-bonds**: Special connections not derived from ResidueType (disulfide bonds, etc.)

Methods for connections:
- `connect_map(Size conn_index)`: Get information about a connection
- `is_bonded(Size other_residue)`: Check if this residue is connected to another
- `connections_to_residue(Size other_residue)`: Get all connections to another residue

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    Res1["Residue 1"] --- Conn1["Polymeric Connection"] --- Res2["Residue 2"]
    Res2 --- Conn2["Polymeric Connection"] --- Res3["Residue 3"]
    Res2 --- Conn3["Branch Connection"] --- Res4["Residue 4 (Branch)"]
    
    subgraph "Connection Map"
        CM1["conn_map(1): Res1-Res2"]
        CM2["conn_map(2): Res2-Res3"]
        CM3["conn_map(3): Res2-Res4"]
    end
```

Sources: [source/src/core/conformation/Residue.hh:1163-1240](source/src/core/conformation/Residue.hh:1163-1240)

## RelationChain to Higher-Level Structures

Residues don't exist in isolation - they are organized into higher-level structures in Rosetta:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    ResidueType --> Residue
    Residue --> Conformation
    Conformation --> Pose
    
    subgraph "Type Level (Templates)"
        ResidueType["ResidueType (Chemical template)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Instance Level (Models)"
        Residue["Residue (Molecular component)"]
        Conformation["Conformation (Collection of residues)"]
        Pose["Pose (Complete molecular model)"]
    end
```

- **Residue** is a single molecular component (amino acid, nucleotide, etc.)
- **Conformation** is a collection of residues with defined spatial relationships
- **Pose** is a complete molecular model that includes a Conformation and additional information (energies, PDB info, etc.)

Sources: [source/src/core/pose/Pose.cc:135-142](source/src/core/pose/Pose.cc:135-142), [source/src/core/conformation/Conformation.cc:126-132](source/src/core/conformation/Conformation.cc:126-132)

## Special Cases and Extensions

Rosetta extends the basic Residue/ResidueType system to handle special cases and more complex molecular structures.

### Carbohydrates

Carbohydrates require special handling due to their complex branching structure and unique chemical properties.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    ResidueType --> CarbohydrateInfo["CarbohydrateInfo"]
    CarbohydrateInfo --> Stereochemistry["Stereochemistry"]
    CarbohydrateInfo --> Anomeric["Anomeric Configuration"]
    CarbohydrateInfo --> RingSize["Ring Size"]
    CarbohydrateInfo --> Modifications["Chemical Modifications"]
    
    ResidueType --- Residue
    Residue --> GlycanNode["GlycanNode"]
    GlycanNode --> GlycanTree["GlycanTree"]
    GlycanTree --> GlycanTreeSet["GlycanTreeSet"]
```

The CarbohydrateInfo class extends ResidueType with carbohydrate-specific information:
- Anomeric configuration (α/β)
- Ring size (furanose/pyranose)
- Stereochemistry (D/L)
- Chemical modifications

Sources: [source/src/core/chemical/carbohydrates/CarbohydrateInfo.cc](source/src/core/chemical/carbohydrates/CarbohydrateInfo.cc), [source/src/core/pose/carbohydrates/util.cc](source/src/core/pose/carbohydrates/util.cc)

### Symmetric Structures

Rosetta handles symmetric structures (proteins with multiple identical subunits) using specialized classes:

- **SymmetricConformation**: An extension of Conformation that enforces symmetry
- **SymmetryInfo**: Stores information about symmetry operations

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Residue --> Conformation
    Conformation --> SymmetricConformation["SymmetricConformation"]
    SymmetryInfo["SymmetryInfo"] --> SymmetricConformation
    
    subgraph "Symmetric Operations"
        SO1["Map master to copies"]
        SO2["Enforce symmetry constraints"]
        SO3["Handle symmetric DOFs"]
    end
    
    SymmetricConformation --> SO1
    SymmetricConformation --> SO2
    SymmetricConformation --> SO3
```

Sources: [source/src/core/conformation/symmetry/SymmetricConformation.cc](source/src/core/conformation/symmetry/SymmetricConformation.cc), [source/src/core/conformation/symmetry/SymmetryInfo.cc](source/src/core/conformation/symmetry/SymmetryInfo.cc)

## Conclusion

The Residue and ResidueType classes form the foundation of Rosetta's molecular representation system. ResidueType defines the chemical properties and ideal geometry of a molecular component, while Residue represents a specific instance with unique coordinates and conformation. Together, they enable Rosetta to model a wide range of molecular structures, from simple peptides to complex macromolecular assemblies.

Understanding these classes is essential for working with Rosetta, whether you're developing new functionality or using existing tools to model and design biomolecules.

---
