This page documents Rosetta's system for representing, manipulating, and modeling carbohydrates (sugars). Carbohydrates play important roles in many biological systems, serving structural and functional purposes. Rosetta provides specialized tools for building, modifying, and analyzing carbohydrate structures both as individual molecules and attached to proteins or other biomolecules.

## Overview of Carbohydrate Representation

Rosetta implements a comprehensive system for handling carbohydrate structures through dedicated classes, utilities, and database files. The system supports creation of monosaccharides, oligosaccharides, and glycosylated proteins, following IUPAC carbohydrate nomenclature and conventions.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Core Representation"
        CarboInfo["CarbohydrateInfo"]
        ResType["ResidueType"]
        Residue["Residue"]
        Pose["Pose"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Management System"
        CIM["CarbohydrateInfoManager"]
        DB["Database Files"]
        PatchSystem["Patching System"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Utility Functions"
        Glyco["Glycosylation"]
        Conf["Conformational Tools"]
        IO["I/O Functions"]
    end
    
    ResType -->|"contains"| CarboInfo
    Residue -->|"based on"| ResType
    Pose -->|"contains"| Residue
    
    CIM -->|"validates/provides data for"| CarboInfo
    DB -->|"configures"| CIM
    PatchSystem -->|"modifies"| ResType
    
    Glyco -->|"manipulates"| Pose
    Conf -->|"manages torsions"| Pose
    IO -->|"reads/writes"| Pose
```

Sources: [source/src/core/chemical/carbohydrates/CarbohydrateInfo.hh](). [source/src/core/chemical/carbohydrates/CarbohydrateInfoManager.hh](). [source/src/core/pose/carbohydrates/util.hh]().

## Carbohydrate Information Architecture

The foundation of carbohydrate representation in Rosetta is the `CarbohydrateInfo` class, which stores detailed information about a carbohydrate residue, including its structural and chemical properties. Every carbohydrate `ResidueType` in Rosetta contains a `CarbohydrateInfo` instance.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class ResidueType {
        +carbohydrate_info() CarbohydrateInfo*
        +properties() ResidueProperties
    }
    
    class CarbohydrateInfo {
        -full_name_ string
        -short_name_ string
        -linkage_notation_ string
        -anomeric_carbon_ uint
        -ring_size_ uint
        -n_carbons_ uint
        -modifications_ map
        +basic_name() string
        +is_aldose() bool
        +is_ketose() bool
        +is_reducing_sugar() bool
        +is_glycoside() bool
        +n_branches() uint
        +branch_point(uint) uint
    }
    
    class CarbohydrateInfoManager {
        +get_instance() CarbohydrateInfoManager*
        +is_valid_sugar_code(string) bool
        +root_from_code(string) string
        +morpheme_from_ring_size(uint) string
        +branch_variant_type_from_position(uint) VariantType
    }
    
    ResidueType --> CarbohydrateInfo : contains
    CarbohydrateInfoManager --> CarbohydrateInfo : manages
```

Sources: [source/src/core/chemical/carbohydrates/CarbohydrateInfo.hh:39-591](). [source/src/core/chemical/carbohydrates/CarbohydrateInfoManager.hh:55-285]().

### Key Properties and Classifications

Carbohydrates in Rosetta are classified by several properties:

| Property Type | Examples | Description |
|---------------|----------|-------------|
| Size | TRIOSE, TETROSE, PENTOSE, HEXOSE, etc. | Number of carbon atoms (3-9) |
| Oxidation | ALDOSE, KETOSE | Whether the sugar has an aldehyde or ketone group |
| Ring Form | FURANOSE, PYRANOSE, etc. | Ring size (5-atom ring, 6-atom ring, etc.) |
| Stereochemistry | L_SUGAR, D_SUGAR | L or D configuration |
| Anomeric Form | ALPHA_SUGAR, BETA_SUGAR | Stereoconfiguration at the anomeric carbon |
| Modifications | AMINO_SUGAR, ACETYLAMINO_SUGAR, etc. | Chemical modifications to the base sugar |

Sources: [source/src/core/chemical/residue_properties/general_properties.list:134-193](). [source/src/core/chemical/carbohydrates/CarbohydrateInfo.hh:92-159]().

## Carbohydrate Database System

Rosetta uses a comprehensive database to manage carbohydrate information. The `CarbohydrateInfoManager` singleton serves as the interface to this database.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Database Files"

        patches["patches/carbohydrates/*.txt"]
    end
    
    subgraph "CarbohydrateInfoManager"
        code_map["code_to_root_map()"]
        ring_map["ring_size_to_morpheme_map()"]
        sugar_mods["sugar_modifications_nomenclature_table()"]
        linkage_conf["linkage_conformers()"]
    end
    
    codes_roots -->|"loaded into"| code_map
    ring_morphemes -->|"loaded into"| ring_map
    mods_table -->|"loaded into"| sugar_mods
    linkage_data -->|"loaded into"| linkage_conf
    
    subgraph "Client Code"
        util["CarbohydrateInfo"]

    ring_map -->|"used by"| util
    sugar_mods -->|"used by"| seq_builder

```

Sources: [source/src/core/chemical/carbohydrates/database_io.cc:45-340](). [source/src/core/chemical/carbohydrates/CarbohydrateInfoManager.cc:38-76]().

### Modification System

Rosetta supports a wide range of carbohydrate modifications through its patching system:

| Modification Type | Description | Example Variant Type |
|-------------------|-------------|----------------------|
| Oxidation | Oxidation of specific positions | URONIC_ACID_VARIANT |
| Reduction | Removal of oxygen (deoxy sugars) | C2_DEOXY_SUGAR |
| Amination | Addition of amino groups | C2_AMINO_SUGAR |
| Acetylation | Addition of acetyl groups | O6_ACETYL_SUGAR |
| Phosphorylation | Addition of phosphate groups | C6_PHOSPHORYLATED_SUGAR |
| Sulfation | Addition of sulfate groups | C6_SULFATED_SUGAR |
| Methylation | Addition of methyl groups | O2_METHYL_SUGAR |

These modifications are applied through a patching system, where patches modify the base sugar residue types.

Sources: [database/chemical/residue_type_sets/fa_standard/patches.txt:166-226](). [source/src/core/chemical/residue_properties/variant_types.list:222-388]().

## Building Carbohydrate Structures

Rosetta provides multiple ways to create carbohydrate structures:

1. From IUPAC-style saccharide sequences
2. By loading PDB files containing carbohydrates
3. By glycosylating existing protein structures

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Creation Methods"
        iupac["IUPAC Sequence"]
        pdb["PDB File"]
        glyco["Glycosylation"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Intermediate Steps"
        res_types["Residue Types"]
        append["Append Residues"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Result"
        pose["Pose with Carbohydrates"]
    end
    
    iupac -->|"residue_types_from_saccharide_sequence()"| res_types
    res_types -->|"append_pose_with_glycan_residues()"| append
    append --> pose
    
    pdb -->|"pose_from_file()"| pose
    
    glyco -->|"glycosylate_pose()"| pose
```

Sources: [source/src/core/pose/annotated_sequence.cc:249-604](). [source/src/core/pose/carbohydrates/util.cc:374-535]().

### Creating from IUPAC Sequences

Rosetta supports creation of carbohydrate structures from IUPAC-style sequences:

```
make_pose_from_saccharide_sequence(pose, "alpha-D-Glcp-(1->4)-alpha-D-Glcp-(1->4)-D-Glcp");
```

The sequence format follows carbohydrate naming conventions:
- Anomer specification: `alpha-` or `beta-`
- Stereochemistry: `L-` or `D-`
- Base name: Three-letter code (e.g., `Glc` for glucose)
- Ring form: `p` for pyranose, `f` for furanose
- Linkage: `(1->4)` indicates a glycosidic bond from C1 of one residue to O4 of the next
- Branches use square brackets: `[alpha-L-Fucp-(1->3)]-` indicates a branch

Sources: [source/src/core/pose/annotated_sequence.cc:226-246](). [source/src/core/pose/annotated_sequence.cc:292-342]().

### Glycosylation

Rosetta can add carbohydrate structures to proteins through glycosylation:

```cpp
// Glycosylate at position 2 with a specific sugar
glycosylate_pose(pose, 2, "ND2", "alpha-D-Glcp-(1->4)-beta-D-GlcpNAc", true);

// Use a shorthand for common glycosylation sites
glycosylate_pose(pose, 2, "alpha-D-Glcp-(1->4)-beta-D-GlcpNAc");

// Load a glycan from a predefined file
glycosylate_pose_by_file(pose, 2, "core_5_O-glycan");
```

The system supports:
- N-linked glycosylation (to Asn residues)
- O-linked glycosylation (to Ser/Thr residues)
- C-linked glycosylation (to Trp residues)
- Custom glycosylation to arbitrary atoms

Sources: [source/src/core/pose/carbohydrates/util.cc:374-489](). [source/src/core/pose/carbohydrates/util.cc:507-585]().

## Manipulating Carbohydrate Structures

Rosetta provides tools for manipulating the conformation of carbohydrate structures, particularly focused on the glycosidic linkages between residues.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Glycosidic Torsions"
        phi["Phi: O5-C1-O1-Cx"]
        psi["Psi: C1-O1-Cx-C(x+1)"]
        omega["Omega: O1-Cx-C(x+1)-O(x+1)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Manipulation Functions"
        get_tor["get_glycosidic_torsion()"]
        set_tor["set_glycosidic_torsion()"]
        ideal["idealize_last_n_glycans_in_pose()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "MoveMap Integration"
        create_mm["create_glycan_movemap_from_residue_selector()"]
        set_chi["set_glycan_iupac_chi_torsions()"]
        set_bb["set_glycan_iupac_bb_torsions()"]
    end
    
    phi --> get_tor
    psi --> get_tor
    omega --> get_tor
    
    get_tor --> set_tor
    set_tor --> ideal
    
    ideal --> create_mm
    create_mm --> set_chi
    create_mm --> set_bb
```

Sources: [source/src/core/pose/carbohydrates/util.cc:219-264](). [source/src/core/pose/carbohydrates/util.hh:222-236]().

### Glycosidic Torsion Angles

Glycosidic linkages between sugars are described by specific torsion angles:

1. **Phi (φ)**: The torsion angle around the C1-O1 bond (typically O5-C1-O1-Cx)
2. **Psi (ψ)**: The torsion angle around the O1-Cx bond (typically C1-O1-Cx-C(x+1))
3. **Omega (ω)**: For 1→6 linkages, additional torsions around C5-C6 (O1-C6-C5-O5)

These can be accessed and modified using:
```cpp
// Get torsion value
Angle phi = get_glycosidic_torsion(phi_dihedral, pose, residue_num);

// Set torsion value
set_glycosidic_torsion(phi_dihedral, pose, residue_num, 60.0);
```

Sources: [source/src/core/pose/carbohydrates/util.cc:161-192](). [source/src/core/pose/carbohydrates/util.cc:227-236]().

### MoveMap Integration

Carbohydrate-specific MoveMaps can be created to control which degrees of freedom are allowed to move during minimization or other conformational changes:

```cpp
// Create a MoveMap for selected carbohydrate residues
MoveMapOP movemap = create_glycan_movemap_from_residue_selector(
    pose, selector, true /*chi*/, false /*ring*/, true /*bb*/);
```

The system distinguishes between:
- IUPAC chi torsions (rotatable hydroxyl groups)
- IUPAC glycosidic torsions (linkages between sugars)
- Ring torsions (sugar pucker conformations)

Sources: [source/src/core/pose/carbohydrates/util.cc:291-344](). [source/src/core/select/movemap/MoveMapFactory.cc:157-180]().

## Working with Carbohydrate Branches

Carbohydrates often have branched structures, which Rosetta handles through special utility functions.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Branch Identification"
        get_branch["get_carbohydrate_residues_of_branch()"]
        get_tips["get_carbohydrate_tips_of_branch()"]
        get_res_tips["get_carbohydrate_residues_and_tips_of_branch()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Branch Manipulation"
        delete_branch["delete_carbohydrate_branch()"]
        delete_leaf["delete_leaf()"]
        remove_variant["remove_carbohydrate_branch_point_variants()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Tree Structure"
        GlycanTreeSet["GlycanTreeSet"]
        GlycanTree["GlycanTree"]
        GlycanNode["GlycanNode"]
    end
    
    get_branch --> get_res_tips
    get_tips --> get_res_tips
    
    get_res_tips --> delete_branch
    get_res_tips --> delete_leaf
    
    GlycanTreeSet -->|"contains"| GlycanTree
    GlycanTree -->|"contains"| GlycanNode
    
    GlycanTreeSet -->|"used by"| get_res_tips
    GlycanNode -->|"used by"| get_branch
```

Sources: [source/src/core/pose/carbohydrates/util.hh:243-262](). [source/src/core/pose/carbohydrates/util.hh:309-381]().

### Branch Traversal

Functions for traversing carbohydrate branches:

```cpp
// Get all residues in a branch starting from a specific residue
utility::vector1<core::Size> residues = get_carbohydrate_residues_of_branch(pose, start_res);

// Get just the terminal residues ("tips") of branches
utility::vector1<core::Size> tips = get_carbohydrate_tips_of_branch(pose, start_res);

// Get both residues and tips as a pair
auto result = get_carbohydrate_residues_and_tips_of_branch(pose, start_res);
utility::vector1<core::Size> all_residues = result.first;
utility::vector1<core::Size> branch_tips = result.second;
```

Sources: [source/src/core/pose/carbohydrates/util.hh:243-262](). [source/src/core/pose/carbohydrates/util.cc:243-262]().

### Branch Manipulation

Functions for modifying branch structures:

```cpp
// Delete an entire branch starting from a specific residue
delete_carbohydrate_branch(pose, branch_start);

// Delete a specific leaf (linear segment ending in a tip)
delete_leaf(pose, leaf_residues);

// Remove branch point variants from a residue
remove_carbohydrate_branch_point_variants(pose, res_num);
```

Sources: [source/src/core/pose/carbohydrates/util.hh:313-381](). [source/src/core/pose/carbohydrates/util.cc:313-381]().

Rosetta provides specialized I/O functionality for carbohydrates to support various file formats and naming conventions.

### Parsing Modifications

When interpreting carbohydrate names with modifications, Rosetta parses complex modification patterns:

```cpp
// Parse "GlcpNAc" into glucose with an N-acetyl group at position 2
utility::vector1<std::pair<core::uint, std::string>> modifications = 
    sugar_modifications_from_suffix("NAc");
// Result: [(2, "NAc")] - position 2, N-acetyl modification
```

The system uses a database table that maps modification codes to their meanings:

| Code | Full Name | Position | Patch Name |
|------|-----------|----------|------------|
| N    | amino     | 2        | NH3+       |
| NAc  | acetylamino | 2      | AcNH       |
| A    | uronic acid | 6      | uronic_acid |
| P    | phosphate | 6        | OPO32-     |
| S    | sulfate  | 6         | OSO3-      |

Sources: [source/src/core/io/carbohydrates/pose_io.cc:55-101](). [database/chemical/carbohydrates/sugar_modifications.table]().

## Conclusion

Rosetta's carbohydrate handling system provides a comprehensive framework for modeling, building, and analyzing carbohydrate structures. The system integrates with Rosetta's core modeling capabilities while providing specialized functionality for the unique properties of carbohydrates.

For working with carbohydrates attached to proteins in scoring functions, see [Scoring System](#3). For manipulating carbohydrates with movers and protocols, see [Protocol System](#4).

The Rosetta I/O System is responsible for reading molecular structure data from files into Pose objects and writing Pose objects back to files. It includes mechanisms for handling various file formats (primarily PDB and mmCIF), processing structural information, resolving residue types, and managing chain connectivity. This document covers the core components of the I/O system and how data flows through it when reading and writing molecular structures.

## Overview

The I/O system serves as a bridge between external file formats and Rosetta's internal representation (Pose objects). The system is designed to handle the complexities of biomolecular structure files, including residue naming, chain identification, atom connectivity, and special molecular features.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Input"
        InputFiles["Structure Files (PDB/mmCIF/etc)"] --> StructFileRep
    end
    
    subgraph "Core Components"
        StructFileRep["StructFileRep"]
        StructFileRepOptions["StructFileRepOptions"]
        StructFileRepOptions --> PoseFromSFRBuilder
        StructFileRepOptions --> PoseToSFRConverter
    end
    
    subgraph "Pose Creation"
        StructFileRep --> PoseFromSFRBuilder["PoseFromSFRBuilder"]
        ResidueTypeSet["ResidueTypeSet"] --> PoseFromSFRBuilder
        PoseFromSFRBuilder --> Pose["Pose"]
        PoseFromSFRBuilder --> MissingAtoms["Missing Atoms Mask"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output"
        Pose --> PoseToSFRConverter["PoseToStructFileRepConverter"]
        PoseToSFRConverter --> StructFileRep2["StructFileRep"]
        StructFileRep2 --> OutputFiles["Structure Files (PDB/mmCIF/etc)"]
    end
```

Sources:
- [source/src/core/io/StructFileRep.hh]()
- [source/src/core/io/StructFileRepOptions.hh]()
- [source/src/core/io/pose_from_sfr/PoseFromSFRBuilder.hh]()
- [source/src/core/io/pose_to_sfr/PoseToStructFileRepConverter.hh]()

## Core Components

### StructFileRep

`StructFileRep` is an intermediate representation of structural data from files. It stores:

- Atom coordinates and properties
- Residue information
- Chain organization
- Header information
- Crystallographic data
- Connectivity information (LINK records)
- Secondary structure annotations

This class serves as a bridge between external file formats and Rosetta's internal data structures, enabling platform-independent storage of structure information.

### StructFileRepOptions

`StructFileRepOptions` controls how structural data is read and written. It provides numerous configuration options:

| Category | Options | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| Chain Handling | `check_if_residues_are_Ntermini`, `check_if_residues_are_Ctermini` | Control which chains have termini |
| Molecule Processing | `ignore_waters`, `ignore_sugars` | Filter out specific molecule types |
| Residue Processing | `fast_restyping`, `ignore_unrecognized_res` | Control residue type assignment |
| Special Features | `auto_detect_glycan_connections` | Handle specialized molecule types |
| Output Controls | `output_virtual`, `output_secondary_structure` | Control what data is included in output |
| File Format | `use_pdb_format_HETNAM_records` | Control format-specific features |

These options allow fine-grained control over how Rosetta reads and writes structural data.

Sources:
- [source/src/core/io/StructFileRepOptions.cc:135-192]()
- [source/src/core/io/StructFileRepOptions.hh:62-122]()

## Reading Structures: Input Flow

When reading a structure file into Rosetta, the data flows through several processing steps:

```mermaid
graph TD
    StructFile["Structure File"] --> StructFileRep["StructFileRep"]
    StructFileRep --> PoseFromSFRBuilder["PoseFromSFRBuilder"]
    
    subgraph "PoseFromSFRBuilder Process"
        Setup["1. Setup"] --> Pass1["2. Split/Merge Residues"]
        Pass1 --> Pass2["3. Resolve Residue Types"]
        Pass2 --> Pass3["4. Verify Backbone Atoms"]
        Pass3 --> Pass4["5. Redo Termini"]
        Pass4 --> Pass5["6. Note Discarded Atoms"]
        Pass5 --> BuildPose["7. Build Initial Pose"]
        BuildPose --> RefinePose["8. Refine Pose"]
    end
    
    PoseFromSFRBuilder --> Setup
    RefinePose --> Pose["Pose"]
    RefinePose --> MissingAtoms["Missing Atoms Mask"]
    
    ResidueTypeSet["ResidueTypeSet"] --> PoseFromSFRBuilder
    Options["StructFileRepOptions"] --> PoseFromSFRBuilder
```

The key steps in this process are:

1. **Setup**: Extract all residue information from the `StructFileRep` and prepare for building the Pose.

2. **Split/Merge Residues**: Handle special cases where residues need to be split (e.g., a residue that should be represented as multiple residues in Rosetta) or merged (e.g., ACE caps being merged with the next residue).

3. **Resolve Residue Types**: Match each residue to the appropriate `ResidueType` in Rosetta's database, handling standard and non-standard residues.

4. **Verify Backbone Atoms**: Ensure that essential backbone atoms are present for proper molecular representation.

5. **Redo Termini**: Process chain termini and ensure they have the correct terminal variants.

6. **Note Discarded Atoms**: Keep track of atoms present in the input file but not included in the Pose.

7. **Build Initial Pose**: Construct the Pose object with the processed residue information.

8. **Refine Pose**: Finalize the Pose, setting up additional information like PDBInfo.

Sources:
- [source/src/core/io/pose_from_sfr/PoseFromSFRBuilder.cc:116-140]()
- [source/src/core/io/pose_from_sfr/PoseFromSFRBuilder.hh:85-98]()

### Special Handling in Reading

#### Nucleic Acid Processing

The I/O system includes special handling for nucleic acids, including:

- Converting PDB-style atom names (with asterisks) to Rosetta-style names (with primes)
- Detecting and handling DNA vs. RNA
- Processing virtual phosphates for 5' terminal residues

```cpp
// Example of nucleic acid name conversion
if ( atom_info.name.size() >= 1 && atom_info.name[atom_info.name.size()-1] == '*' ) {
    std::string new_atom_name = atom_info.name.substr(0,atom_info.name.size()-1) + "\'";
    rinfo.rename_atom( original_atom_name, new_atom_name );
}
```

#### Chain Breaks and Connectivity

The system automatically detects chain breaks based on:
- Different chain IDs
- Missing connecting atoms
- Atom distances exceeding expected bond lengths
- Presence of `CUTPOINT_LOWER` and `CUTPOINT_UPPER` variants

Sources:
- [source/src/core/io/pose_from_sfr/PoseFromSFRBuilder.cc:158-213]()
- [source/src/core/pose/rna/util.cc:246-313]()

## Writing Structures: Output Flow

When writing a Pose to a structure file, the data flows through these steps:

```mermaid
graph TD
    Pose["Pose"] --> PoseToSFRConverter["PoseToStructFileRepConverter"]
    Options["StructFileRepOptions"] --> PoseToSFRConverter
    
    subgraph "PoseToStructFileRepConverter Process"
        InitFromPose["1. Initialize from Pose"] --> GetHeader["2. Get Header Information"]
        GetHeader --> GetCrystInfo["3. Get Crystallographic Info"]
        GetCrystInfo --> GetSecStruct["4. Generate Secondary Structure"]
        GetSecStruct --> CollectData["5. Collect Additional Data"]
        CollectData --> ProcessResidues["6. Process Residues and Atoms"]
        ProcessResidues --> SetupConnectivity["7. Setup Connectivity"]
    end
    
    PoseToSFRConverter --> InitFromPose
    SetupConnectivity --> StructFileRep["StructFileRep"]
    
    StructFileRep --> Writers["File Writers"]
    Writers --> OutputFiles["Structure Files"]
```

The steps in this process are:

1. **Initialize from Pose**: Extract basic data from the Pose and create a new `StructFileRep`.

2. **Get Header Information**: Set up title section records (HEADER, TITLE, AUTHOR, etc.).

3. **Get Crystallographic Info**: Set up crystallographic information if available.

4. **Generate Secondary Structure**: Create HELIX and SHEET records if required.

5. **Collect Additional Data**: Gather extra information like membrane topology or energy terms.

6. **Process Residues and Atoms**: Convert each residue and atom from the Pose to the appropriate representation in `StructFileRep`.

7. **Setup Connectivity**: Add LINK and SSBOND records based on residue connectivity.

Sources:
- [source/src/core/io/pose_to_sfr/PoseToStructFileRepConverter.cc:199-309]()
- [source/src/core/io/pose_to_sfr/PoseToStructFileRepConverter.hh:112-113]()

### Atom and Residue Processing

For each residue and atom in the Pose, the converter:

1. Creates a `ResidueInformation` object with chain ID, residue number, name, etc.
2. For each atom, creates an `AtomInformation` object with coordinates, name, element, etc.
3. Handles special properties like alternate conformations, occupancy, and temperature factors
4. Determines whether atoms should be represented as ATOM or HETATM records

```cpp
// Simplified atom processing logic
AtomInformation ai;
ai.isHet = !rsd.type().has_property(CANONICAL_AA);
ai.chainID = res_info.chainID();
ai.resSeq = res_info.resSeq();
ai.name = rsd.atom_name(atom_index);
ai.x = atom.xyz()(1);
ai.y = atom.xyz()(2);
ai.z = atom.xyz()(3);
```

Sources:
- [source/src/core/io/pose_to_sfr/PoseToStructFileRepConverter.cc:461-516]()

## File Format Support

Rosetta's I/O system primarily supports three file formats:

### PDB Format

The Protein Data Bank (PDB) format is the most widely used format. The `pdb_writer` module:

- Creates proper PDB record types (ATOM, HETATM, LINK, etc.)
- Formats coordinates and atom information according to PDB specifications
- Handles special features like multiple models and biological assemblies

```mermaid
graph TD
    StructFileRep["StructFileRep"] --> RecordCreation["Create Records"]
    RecordCreation --> FormatRecords["Format Records as PDB Lines"]
    FormatRecords --> OutputFile["Write to PDB File"]
    
    subgraph "PDB Record Types"
        HEADER["HEADER/TITLE/etc"]
        REMARK["REMARK"]
        HELIX["HELIX/SHEET"]
        ATOM["ATOM/HETATM"]
        LINK["LINK/SSBOND"]
        TER["TER"]
        END["END"]
    end
    
    RecordCreation --> HEADER
    RecordCreation --> REMARK
    RecordCreation --> HELIX
    RecordCreation --> ATOM
    RecordCreation --> LINK
    RecordCreation --> TER
    RecordCreation --> END
```

Sources:
- [source/src/core/io/pdb/pdb_writer.cc:297-342]()

### mmCIF Format

The macromolecular Crystallographic Information File (mmCIF) format is a more structured alternative to PDB:

- Uses tag-value pairs organized into data categories
- Has fewer limitations than PDB (no atom name/residue number size restrictions)
- Stores more comprehensive metadata

### Silent File Format

Rosetta's native "silent file" format is a compact binary format designed for storing multiple structures efficiently:

- More space-efficient than PDB for storing many structures
- Preserves Rosetta-specific information (scores, sequence mapping, etc.)
- Used extensively for large-scale simulations and analysis

## Special Features

### Chain and Terminus Management

The I/O system includes sophisticated chain detection and terminus management:

- Automatically identifies chain breaks based on connectivity and chain IDs
- Controls which chains have N- and C-termini via options
- Handles special cases like circular peptides and non-standard termini

```cpp
// Simplified terminus detection logic
bool is_lower_terminus = (i == 1 || !same_chain_prev) && 
    check_Ntermini_for_this_chain && 
    !lower_terminus_is_occupied_according_to_link_map(resid);
bool is_upper_terminus = (i == nres_pdb || !same_chain_next) && 
    check_Ctermini_for_this_chain && 
    !upper_terminus_is_occupied_according_to_link_map(resid);
```

Sources:
- [source/src/core/io/pose_from_sfr/PoseFromSFRBuilder.cc:446-448]()

### Missing Atom Handling

When atoms are missing in the input file, the system:

1. Tracks which atoms are missing using an `AtomID_Mask`
2. Can build coordinates for missing atoms based on ideal geometry
3. Can randomize coordinates for missing atoms if requested

### Specialized Residue Handling

The system includes specialized handling for:

- Nucleic acids (RNA/DNA)
- Non-canonical amino acids (D-amino acids, beta-amino acids)
- Carbohydrates and glycans
- Modified residues (phosphorylated, acetylated, etc.)
- Ligands and non-standard residues

Sources:
- [source/src/core/io/pose_from_sfr/PoseFromSFRBuilder.cc:158-213]()
- [source/src/core/chemical/AA.cc:36-129]()

## Summary

The Rosetta I/O System provides a flexible and extensible framework for reading and writing molecular structures in various formats. It handles the complexities of biomolecular representation, residue typing, chain connectivity, and special features. The system's modular design separates concerns between file parsing, data representation, and Pose construction, making it adaptable to different file formats and structural features.

The primary workflow involves:
1. Reading structure files into the intermediate `StructFileRep` representation
2. Converting between `StructFileRep` and Pose objects using the builder and converter classes
3. Writing Pose objects back to various file formats

This architecture allows Rosetta to support a wide range of structural biology applications, from reading experimental structures to writing simulation results and designs.

The Rosetta Scoring System evaluates the energy (or "score") of molecular structures by combining weighted energy terms that model various physical interactions. This system is central to virtually all Rosetta applications including structure prediction, protein design, and molecular docking, as it provides the energetic evaluation that guides conformational sampling toward physically realistic structures.

## Scoring System Architecture

The scoring system combines multiple weighted energy terms to evaluate the energy of a molecular structure represented as a Pose. The architecture consists of several key components that work together to calculate and manage energy evaluations.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Score Function Components"
        ScoreFunction["ScoreFunction"]
        Weights["Weights Map"]
        ScoreType["ScoreType Enum"]
        EnergyMap["EnergyMap"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Energy Method Framework"
        EnergyMethod["EnergyMethod Interface"]
        EM_Types["Energy Method Types"]
        EM_Types --> |"includes"| OneBody["One-Body Methods"]
        EM_Types --> |"includes"| TwoBodyCI["Context-Independent Two-Body"]
        EM_Types --> |"includes"| TwoBodyCD["Context-Dependent Two-Body"]
        EM_Types --> |"includes"| WholeStructure["Whole-Structure Methods"]
        EnergyMethodOptions["EnergyMethodOptions"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Management"
        ScoringManager["ScoringManager"]
        EnergyMethodFactory["Energy Method Factory"]
        ScoreTypeManager["ScoreTypeManager"]
    end
    
    ScoreFunction --> |"contains"| Weights
    ScoreFunction --> |"uses"| EnergyMap
    ScoreFunction --> |"evaluates with"| EnergyMethod
    
    ScoreType --> |"identifies"| EnergyMethod
    ScoreTypeManager --> |"manages"| ScoreType
    
    EnergyMethod --> |"configured by"| EnergyMethodOptions
    
    ScoringManager --> |"creates/manages"| EnergyMethod
    ScoringManager --> |"uses"| EnergyMethodFactory
    
    Pose[/"Pose"/] --> |"scored by"| ScoreFunction
    Energies["Energies"] --> |"stored in"| Pose
    ScoreFunction --> |"populates"| Energies

    classDef core fill:#f5f5f5,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px;
    class ScoreFunction,EnergyMethod,ScoringManager core;
```

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/ScoreFunction.hh](), [source/src/core/scoring/methods/EnergyMethod.hh](), [source/src/core/scoring/ScoringManager.hh](), [source/src/core/scoring/ScoreType.hh]()

## Core Components

### ScoreType and ScoreTypeManager

`ScoreType` is an enum that defines all possible energy terms in Rosetta. These terms represent different physical interactions such as van der Waals forces, electrostatics, hydrogen bonding, etc.

The `ScoreTypeManager` handles the mapping between string names (e.g., "fa_atr") and the corresponding `ScoreType` enum values, allowing for convenient access through string identifiers.

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "ScoreType Categories"
        CI2B["Context-Independent Two-Body"]
        CD2B["Context-Dependent Two-Body"]
        CI1B["Context-Independent One-Body"]
        WS["Whole-Structure"]
    end
    
    CI2B --> |"examples"| CI2B_Examples["fa_atr, fa_rep, fa_sol"]
    CD2B --> |"examples"| CD2B_Examples["hbond_sr_bb, hbond_sc"]
    CI1B --> |"examples"| CI1B_Examples["rama, omega, fa_dun"]
    WS --> |"examples"| WS_Examples["rg, cart_bonded"]
    
    ScoreTypeManager["ScoreTypeManager"] --> |"maps names to"| ScoreType["ScoreType Enum"]
    ScoreType --> CI2B
    ScoreType --> CD2B
    ScoreType --> CI1B
    ScoreType --> WS
```

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/ScoreType.hh](), [source/src/core/scoring/ScoreTypeManager.cc]()

The score types are organized into categories based on their computational characteristics:

1. **Context-Independent Two-Body Terms**: Interactions between pairs of atoms/residues that don't depend on the surrounding environment (e.g., van der Waals)
2. **Context-Dependent Two-Body Terms**: Interactions that depend on the surrounding environment (e.g., hydrogen bonds)
3. **Context-Independent One-Body Terms**: Properties of individual residues (e.g., torsional preferences)
4. **Whole-Structure Terms**: Properties of the entire structure (e.g., radius of gyration)

### ScoreFunction

The `ScoreFunction` class combines multiple energy terms with weights to calculate a total energy score. It maintains a map of weights for each score term and coordinates the evaluation of all energy terms.

Common predefined score functions include:
- **REF2015**: The standard full-atom score function for protein structure prediction and design
- **beta_nov16**: A variant of REF2015 with optimized parameters for beta-sheet proteins
- **talaris2014**: An older score function that preceded REF2015

```mermaid
graph TD
    ScoreFunction["ScoreFunction"] --> |"manages"| Weights["Weights Map<ScoreType, weight>"]
    ScoreFunction --> |"calls"| EnergyMethods["Energy Methods"]
    ScoreFunction --> |"stores results in"| EnergyMap["EnergyMap"]
    
    subgraph "ScoreFunction Operations"
        score["score(pose)"]
        score_typed["score_with_type(pose, ScoreType)"]
        partial_score["partial_score(pose, subset)"]
        set_weight["set_weight(ScoreType, weight)"]
        get_weight["get_weight(ScoreType)"]
    end
    
    ScoreFunction --> score
    ScoreFunction --> score_typed
    ScoreFunction --> partial_score
    ScoreFunction --> set_weight
    ScoreFunction --> get_weight
    
    score --> |"returns"| TotalEnergy["Total Energy (Real)"]
    score --> |"populates"| PoseEnergies["pose.energies()"]
```

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/ScoreFunction.hh](), [source/src/core/scoring/ScoreFunctionFactory.hh]()

### ScoringManager and Energy Methods

The `ScoringManager` is the central singleton that handles creation and management of energy methods. It uses lazy loading to create energy methods on-demand, ensuring thread-safety for parallel computation.

`EnergyMethod` is the base interface for all energy calculation implementations. Different energy terms are implemented as derived classes of this interface. The `EnergyMethodOptions` class provides configuration options for energy methods.

```mermaid
graph TD
    ScoringManager["ScoringManager (Singleton)"] --> |"creates/manages"| EnergyMethods["Energy Methods"]
    
    EnergyMethods --> OneBodyMethods["One-Body Methods"]
    EnergyMethods --> TwoBodyMethods["Two-Body Methods"]
    EnergyMethods --> WholeStructureMethods["Whole-Structure Methods"]
    
    OneBodyMethods --> |"examples"| RamaMethod["RamachandranEnergy"]
    OneBodyMethods --> |"examples"| DunMethod["DunbrackEnergy"]
    
    TwoBodyMethods --> |"examples"| VdWMethod["VDW_Energy"]
    TwoBodyMethods --> |"examples"| HBondMethod["HBondEnergy"]
    TwoBodyMethods --> |"examples"| FACTSMethod["FACTSEnergy"]
    
    WholeStructureMethods --> |"examples"| RGMethod["RG_Energy"]
    
    EnergyMethodOptions["EnergyMethodOptions"] --> |"configures"| EnergyMethods
    
    ScoringManager --> |"uses"| EnergyMethodCreators["Energy Method Creators"]
    EnergyMethodCreators --> |"register with"| ScoringManager
```

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/ScoringManager.hh](), [source/src/core/scoring/methods/EnergyMethod.hh](), [source/src/core/scoring/methods/EnergyMethodOptions.hh](), [source/src/core/init/init.cc]()

## Common Energy Terms

The Rosetta scoring system includes numerous energy terms modeling different physical phenomena:

| Term Category | Common Terms | Description |
|---------------|--------------|-------------|
| Van der Waals | fa_atr, fa_rep | Attractive and repulsive components of van der Waals interactions |
| Solvation | fa_sol, lk_ball | Implicit solvation models for water interactions |
| Electrostatics | fa_elec | Electrostatic interactions between charged atoms |
| Hydrogen Bonding | hbond_sr_bb, hbond_lr_bb, hbond_sc | Hydrogen bond interactions with different geometric configurations |
| Torsional | rama, omega, fa_dun | Preferences for backbone and sidechain torsion angles |
| Reference | ref | Per-residue reference energies to balance amino acid preferences |
| Specialized | membrane, carbohydrate, RNA terms | Terms specific to certain molecular types |

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/ScoreType.hh](), [source/src/core/scoring/ScoreTypeManager.cc]()

## FACTS Solvation Model

The Fast Analytical Continuum Treatment of Solvation (FACTS) is an important implicit solvation model in Rosetta. It calculates solvation energies by analytically approximating the continuum solvent model without expensive numerical solutions of the Poisson-Boltzmann equation.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "FACTS Components"
        FACTSPotential["FACTSPotential"]
        FACTSPose["FACTSPose"]
        FACTSResidue["FACTSResidue"]
    end
    
    FACTSPotential --> |"creates"| FACTSPose
    FACTSPose --> |"contains"| FACTSResidue
    
    subgraph "FACTS Energy Calculation"
        Electrostatic["Electrostatic Energy"]
        Nonpolar["Nonpolar Energy"]
        TotalSolvation["Total Solvation Energy"]
    end
    
    FACTSPotential --> |"calculates"| Electrostatic
    FACTSPotential --> |"calculates"| Nonpolar
    Electrostatic --> |"contributes to"| TotalSolvation
    Nonpolar --> |"contributes to"| TotalSolvation
    
    Parameters["FACTS Parameters"] --> |"configure"| FACTSPotential
    AtomParamFile["facts_born_params.epm1.txt"] --> Parameters
```

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSPotential.cc](), [source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSResidue.cc](), [database/chemical/atom_type_sets/fa_standard/extras/facts_born_params.epm1.txt]()

## Energy Method Registration and Initialization

Energy methods are registered during Rosetta startup. The registration process uses a factory pattern to allow the system to create energy methods on demand.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Initialization Process"
        AppInit["Rosetta Initialization"]
        RegisterEM["Register Energy Methods"]
        InitSM["Initialize ScoringManager"]
    end
    
    AppInit --> RegisterEM
    RegisterEM --> InitSM

        EnergyMethodCreator["EnergyMethodCreator"]
    end
    
    RegisterEM --> |"uses"| EnergyMethodRegistrator
    EnergyMethodRegistrator --> |"registers"| EnergyMethodCreator
    EnergyMethodCreator --> |"with"| ScoringManager["ScoringManager"]
    
    subgraph "Examples"
        RegVDW["VDW_EnergyCreator_registrator"]
        RegHBond["HBondEnergyCreator_registrator"]
        RegFacts["FACTSEnergyCreator_registrator"]
    end
    
    EnergyMethodRegistrator --> RegVDW
    EnergyMethodRegistrator --> RegHBond
    EnergyMethodRegistrator --> RegFacts
```

Sources: [source/src/core/init/init.cc](), [source/src/core/scoring/methods/EnergyMethodRegistrator.hh]()

## Using the Scoring System

### Creating and Accessing ScoreFunctions

```cpp
// Create a score function using a predefined type
core::scoring::ScoreFunctionOP scorefxn = core::scoring::get_score_function();  // Default (REF2015)
core::scoring::ScoreFunctionOP custom_scorefxn = core::scoring::ScoreFunctionFactory::create_score_function("ref2015");

// Modify weights
custom_scorefxn->set_weight(core::scoring::fa_atr, 1.0);
custom_scorefxn->set_weight(core::scoring::fa_rep, 0.55);

// Get a weight
double atr_weight = custom_scorefxn->get_weight(core::scoring::fa_atr);
```

### Scoring a Pose

```cpp
// Score an entire pose
double total_energy = scorefxn->score(pose);

// Access energies stored in the pose
core::scoring::Energies const & energies = pose.energies();
double fa_atr_energy = energies.total_energies()[core::scoring::fa_atr];

// Score only a subset of residues
utility::vector1<core::Size> residues_to_score;
residues_to_score.push_back(5);
residues_to_score.push_back(6);
double partial_energy = scorefxn->eval_ci_2b(pose, residues_to_score);
```

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/ScoreFunction.hh](), [source/src/core/scoring/ScoreFunctionFactory.hh]()

## Integration with Other Systems

The scoring system integrates with other Rosetta components including:

1. **Pose System**: Scores are calculated for Pose objects and stored in their Energies component
2. **Protocol System**: Protocols use scoring to evaluate and select conformations
3. **Packing System**: During sidechain packing, scorefunctions guide optimal rotamer selection
4. **Minimization**: Gradient-based minimization uses the scoring system to find local energy minima

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Scoring System"
        ScoreFunction["ScoreFunction"]
        EnergyMethods["Energy Methods"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Pose System"
        Pose["Pose"]
        Energies["Energies"]
        Conformation["Conformation"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Protocol System"
        Movers["Movers"]
        Filters["Filters"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Optimization Systems"
        Packer["Packer"]
        Minimizer["Minimizer"]
    end
    
    ScoreFunction --- |"scores"| Pose
    ScoreFunction --- |"uses"| EnergyMethods
    Pose --- |"contains"| Energies
    Pose --- |"contains"| Conformation
    
    Movers --- |"manipulate"| Pose
    Movers --- |"evaluate with"| ScoreFunction
    Filters --- |"evaluate with"| ScoreFunction
    
    Packer --- |"evaluates with"| ScoreFunction
    Packer --- |"modifies"| Pose
    Minimizer --- |"gradients from"| ScoreFunction
    Minimizer --- |"optimizes"| Pose
```

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/ScoreFunction.hh](), [source/src/core/pose/Pose.hh]()

## Extending the Scoring System

New energy terms can be added to Rosetta by:

1. Adding a new ScoreType enum value in [core/scoring/ScoreType.hh]()
2. Registering the name in [core/scoring/ScoreTypeManager.cc]()
3. Implementing a new EnergyMethod derived class
4. Creating an EnergyMethodCreator for the new method
5. Registering the creator with ScoringManager during initialization

Custom energy terms can also be implemented through PyRosetta using the Python interface.

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/methods/EnergyMethod.hh](), [source/src/core/init/init.cc]()

# Page: Score Function and Energy Methods

# Score Function and Energy Methods

<details>

This page documents Rosetta's scoring system, which is responsible for evaluating the energy of molecular structures. The scoring system is a fundamental component that enables Rosetta to discriminate between good and bad structures during modeling, design, and analysis processes.

## Scoring System Overview

Rosetta's scoring system revolves around the `ScoreFunction` class, which combines multiple weighted energy terms to calculate the total energy of a molecular structure. Each energy term (referred to as an "Energy Method") models a different physical or chemical aspect of the molecule, such as van der Waals interactions, hydrogen bonding, or electrostatic forces.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Core Components"
        ScoreFunction["ScoreFunction"]
        Weights["Weights"]
        EnergyMap["EnergyMap"]
        ScoringManager["ScoringManager"]
        EnergyMethod["EnergyMethod Interface"]
        EnergyMethodOptions["EnergyMethodOptions"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Energy Method Types"
        CI2B["Context-Independent Two-Body"]
        CD2B["Context-Dependent Two-Body"]
        OB["One-Body"]
        WB["Whole-Body"]
    end
    
    ScoreFunction --> Weights
    ScoreFunction --> EnergyMap
    ScoreFunction --> ScoringManager
    ScoringManager --> EnergyMethod
    EnergyMethodOptions --> EnergyMethod
    
    EnergyMethod --> CI2B
    EnergyMethod --> CD2B
    EnergyMethod --> OB
    EnergyMethod --> WB
    
    CI2B --> fa_atr["fa_atr (LJ Attraction)"]
    CI2B --> fa_rep["fa_rep (LJ Repulsion)"]
    CI2B --> fa_sol["fa_sol (Solvation)"]
    
    CD2B --> hbond["hbond (H-bonding)"]
    CD2B --> fa_pair["fa_pair (AA Pair Potential)"]
    
    OB --> rama["rama (Ramachandran)"]
    OB --> omega["omega (Omega Torsion)"]
    OB --> fa_dun["fa_dun (Dunbrack)"]
    
    WB --> rg["rg (Radius of Gyration)"]
    WB --> co["co (Contact Order)"]
```

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/ScoreFunction.hh], [source/src/core/scoring/ScoreType.hh], [source/src/core/scoring/ScoringManager.hh], [source/src/core/scoring/methods/EnergyMethodOptions.hh]

## Core Components

### ScoreFunction

The `ScoreFunction` class is the central component that manages the collection of energy terms and their weights. It provides methods to:

- Evaluate the energy of a molecular structure (Pose)
- Apply different weights to various energy terms
- Calculate energy derivatives for optimization
- Display the energy breakdown by term

The `ScoreFunction` uses the `ScoringManager` to access specific energy methods and an `EnergyMap` to store the calculated energy values.

### ScoreType

Rosetta defines a comprehensive enumeration of all possible energy terms in the `ScoreType` enum. Some of the most commonly used terms include:

| ScoreType | Description | Category |
|-----------|-------------|----------|
| fa_atr | Lennard-Jones attractive | Context-Independent Two-Body |
| fa_rep | Lennard-Jones repulsive | Context-Independent Two-Body |
| fa_sol | Lazaridis-Karplus solvation | Context-Independent Two-Body |
| fa_elec | Coulombic electrostatics | Context-Independent Two-Body |
| hbond_sr_bb | Short-range backbone H-bonds | Context-Dependent Two-Body |
| hbond_lr_bb | Long-range backbone H-bonds | Context-Dependent Two-Body |
| hbond_bb_sc | Backbone-sidechain H-bonds | Context-Dependent Two-Body |
| hbond_sc | Sidechain-sidechain H-bonds | Context-Dependent Two-Body |
| rama | Ramachandran preferences | One-Body |
| p_aa_pp | Probability of amino acid given phi/psi | One-Body |
| fa_dun | Dunbrack rotamer library energy | One-Body |
| ref | Reference energy for amino acids | One-Body |

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/ScoreType.hh:35-760]

### EnergyMethod

The `EnergyMethod` interface defines how energy terms calculate their contributions. All energy terms in Rosetta are implemented as classes that inherit from this interface. Key methods include:

- `evaluate_energy(pose, energies)`: Calculates the energy contribution for a given pose
- `finalize_total_energy(pose, energies)`: Performs post-processing after all energies are calculated

Energy methods are categorized by their context-dependency and the number of bodies they consider.

### EnergyMethodOptions

The `EnergyMethodOptions` class provides a centralized collection of parameters that control how energy methods calculate their energies. These options include:

- Electrostatics parameters (dielectric constant, cutoffs)
- Van der Waals parameters
- Hydrogen bonding criteria
- Solvation model settings
- Many other specialized parameters

Options can be set programmatically or via command-line flags.

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/methods/EnergyMethodOptions.hh], [source/src/core/scoring/methods/EnergyMethodOptions.cc:72-202]

### ScoringManager

The `ScoringManager` is a singleton class that manages the registration and creation of energy methods. It handles:

- Creating energy methods on demand
- Lazy loading of data required by energy methods
- Managing shared resources between energy methods

The `ScoringManager` uses a factory pattern where each energy term has a corresponding `EnergyMethodCreator` class that knows how to instantiate the energy method.

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/ScoringManager.cc:142-799], [source/src/core/scoring/ScoringManager.hh]

## Energy Method Types

Energy methods in Rosetta are categorized based on how they calculate energy:

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Energy Methods"
        EnergyMethod["EnergyMethod Interface"]
        
        CI2B["Context-Independent Two-Body"]
        CD2B["Context-Dependent Two-Body"]
        OB["Context-Independent One-Body"]
        COB["Context-Dependent One-Body"]
        WB["Whole-Body"]
        
        EnergyMethod --> CI2B
        EnergyMethod --> CD2B
        EnergyMethod --> OB
        EnergyMethod --> COB
        EnergyMethod --> WB
    end
    
    subgraph "Implementation Classes"
        CI2B --> TwoBodyEnergy["TwoBodyEnergy"]
        CI2B --> ContextIndependentTwoBodyEnergy["ContextIndependentTwoBodyEnergy"]
        CD2B --> ContextDependentTwoBodyEnergy["ContextDependentTwoBodyEnergy"]
        OB --> OneBodyEnergy["OneBodyEnergy"]
        COB --> ContextDependentOneBodyEnergy["ContextDependentOneBodyEnergy"]
        WB --> WholeStructureEnergy["WholeStructureEnergy"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Example Energy Terms"
        ContextIndependentTwoBodyEnergy --> fa_atr["fa_atr"]
        ContextIndependentTwoBodyEnergy --> fa_rep["fa_rep"]
        ContextDependentTwoBodyEnergy --> hbond["hbond"]
        OneBodyEnergy --> rama["rama"]
        ContextDependentOneBodyEnergy --> fa_dun["fa_dun"]
        WholeStructureEnergy --> rg["rg"]
    end
```

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/ScoreType.hh:35-760], [source/src/core/scoring/methods/EnergyMethod.hh]

### Context-Independent Two-Body Energy Methods

These methods calculate energy between pairs of atoms or residues without considering the broader molecular context. They are typically used for basic physical interactions like:

- `fa_atr`: Lennard-Jones attraction
- `fa_rep`: Lennard-Jones repulsion
- `fa_sol`: Lazaridis-Karplus solvation
- `fa_elec`: Coulombic electrostatics

### Context-Dependent Two-Body Energy Methods

These methods take into account the surrounding molecular environment when calculating pair interactions. Examples include:

- `hbond_sc`: Sidechain-sidechain hydrogen bonds
- `fa_pair`: Knowledge-based pair potential
- `ch_bond`: Carbon-hydrogen bonds

### One-Body Energy Methods

These methods calculate energy based on individual residues:

- `rama`: Ramachandran preferences
- `fa_dun`: Dunbrack rotamer energy
- `p_aa_pp`: Probability of amino acid given phi/psi
- `omega`: Omega torsion potential

### Whole-Body Energy Methods

These methods consider the entire structure to calculate their energy contribution:

- `rg`: Radius of gyration
- `co`: Contact order
- `holes`: Packing quality

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/ScoreType.hh:35-357], [source/src/core/energy_methods/]

## Initialization and Registration Process

Energy methods in Rosetta are registered with the `ScoringManager` using a factory pattern. This process starts at application initialization:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant App as Application
    participant Init as core::init::init()
    participant SMR as EnergyMethodRegistrator
    participant SM as ScoringManager
    participant EMC as EnergyMethodCreator
    participant EM as EnergyMethod
    
    App->>Init: Initialize Rosetta
    Init->>SMR: Static initialization
    SMR->>SM: Register EnergyMethodCreator
    
    Note over App,SM: Later during execution...
    
    App->>SM: get_energy_method(ScoreType)
    
    alt Energy method not yet created
        SM->>EMC: create_energy_method()
        EMC->>EM: Instantiate
        EM->>SM: Return new instance
    end
    
    SM->>App: Return energy method
```

The registration process happens through static initialization in `core/init/init.cc`, where each energy method creator is registered with the `ScoringManager` through an `EnergyMethodRegistrator`.

Sources: [source/src/core/init/init.cc:440-510], [source/src/core/scoring/ScoringManager.cc:442-509]

## Common Usage Patterns

### Creating a ScoreFunction

```cpp
// Get the default score function
ScoreFunctionOP score_function = core::scoring::get_score_function();

// Get a specific named score function
ScoreFunctionOP score_function = core::scoring::get_score_function("ref2015");
```

### Evaluating Energy

```cpp
// Score an entire pose
Real energy = score_function->score(pose);

// Get the breakdown of energy terms
EnergyMap energies = pose.energies().total_energies();
```

### Setting Weights

```cpp
// Set the weight for a specific energy term
score_function->set_weight(fa_atr, 0.8);

// Zero the weight for an energy term
score_function->set_weight(fa_elec, 0.0);
```

### Creating Custom Score Functions

```cpp
// Create an empty score function
ScoreFunctionOP score_function = utility::pointer::make_shared<ScoreFunction>();

// Add energy terms with weights
score_function->set_weight(fa_atr, 1.0);
score_function->set_weight(fa_rep, 0.55);
score_function->set_weight(fa_sol, 1.0);
score_function->set_weight(hbond_sr_bb, 1.0);
```

## Advanced Topics

### Adding Custom Energy Methods

To add a custom energy method to Rosetta:

1. Create a new class that inherits from the appropriate `EnergyMethod` base class
2. Implement the `evaluate_energy` and `finalize_total_energy` methods
3. Create an `EnergyMethodCreator` class for your energy method
4. Register your creator with the `ScoringManager` using an `EnergyMethodRegistrator`

### Energy Method Options

The `EnergyMethodOptions` class provides extensive customization of energy calculation parameters. Some examples include:

- Electrostatics parameters:
  ```cpp
  options.exclude_protein_protein_fa_elec(true);
  options.elec_max_dis(5.5);
  options.elec_min_dis(1.6);
  options.elec_die(10.0);
  ```

- Hydrogen bonding parameters:
  ```cpp
  options.hbond_options()->exclude_bb_bb(false);
  options.hbond_options()->smooth_hb_potential(true);
  ```

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/methods/EnergyMethodOptions.cc:72-202], [source/src/core/scoring/methods/EnergyMethodOptions.hh]

# Page: FACTS Solvation Model

# FACTS Solvation Model

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [database/chemical/atom_type_sets/fa_standard/extras/facts_born_params.epm1.txt](database/chemical/atom_type_sets/fa_standard/extras/facts_born_params.epm1.txt)
- [database/scoring/weights/scorefacts_cart.wts](database/scoring/weights/scorefacts_cart.wts)
- [source/doc/options.dox](source/doc/options.dox)
- [source/src/basic/options/options_rosetta.py](source/src/basic/options/options_rosetta.py)
- [source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSPotential.cc](source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSPotential.cc)
- [source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSPotential.hh](source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSPotential.hh)
- [source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSResidue.cc](source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSResidue.cc)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This document describes the FACTS (Fast Analytical Continuum Treatment of Solvation) model implemented in Rosetta. FACTS is an implicit solvent model used to efficiently calculate the solvation free energy of biomolecules. It provides an analytical approximation for both polar (electrostatic) and non-polar (surface area) contributions to solvation. 

The FACTS model is a critical component of Rosetta's scoring system when considering solvent effects during protein modeling, design, and energy calculations. For more information about the general scoring systems in Rosetta, see [Score Function and Energy Methods](#3.1).

## Overview

FACTS uses an analytical approach to calculate solvation energies without explicitly representing water molecules, making it computationally efficient compared to explicit solvent models. It approximates the Born radii for each atom and calculates solvation free energies based on these radii and solvent accessible surface areas (SASA).

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "FACTS Energy Components"
        Polar["Polar Component (Electrostatic)"]
        NonPolar["Non-Polar Component (Surface Area)"]
        Total["Total Solvation Energy"]
    end
    
    subgraph "FACTS Parameters"
        BR["Born Radii"]
        SASA["Solvent Accessible Surface Area"]
        AtomParams["Atom-Specific Parameters"]
    end
    
    subgraph "FACTS Calculations"
        Burial["Atom Burial Calculation"]
        SelfTerms["Self-Term Calculation"]
        PairwiseTerms["Pairwise Interaction Calculation"]
    end
    
    Burial --> BR
    Burial --> SASA
    AtomParams --> Burial
    AtomParams --> SelfTerms
    AtomParams --> PairwiseTerms
    
    BR --> Polar
    SASA --> NonPolar
    
    Polar --> Total
    NonPolar --> Total
    
    SelfTerms --> Polar
    PairwiseTerms --> Polar
```

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSPotential.cc](), [source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSResidue.cc]()

## Architecture and Class Hierarchy

The FACTS model implementation in Rosetta consists of several interrelated classes that handle different aspects of the solvation calculation.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class FACTSPotential {
        -FACTSRsdTypeMap FACTSrsdtypemap_
        -Real MultiplicitiveFactor_
        -Real inv_die_
        -Real Tau_
        -Real Kappa_
        -Real GBpair_cut_
        +setup_for_scoring()
        +evaluate_polar_energy()
        +evaluate_nonpolar_energy()
        +calculate_GBpair_exact()
        +calculate_GBpair_fast()
    }
    
    class FACTSPoseInfo {
        -vector~FACTSResidueInfo~ residue_info_
        +initialize()
        +residue_info()
        +update_enumeration_shell()
    }
    
    class FACTSResidueInfo {
        -FACTSRsdTypeInfoCOP restypeinfo_
        -vector~Real~ Ai_
        -vector~Real~ Bi_
        -vector~Real~ BR_
        -vector~Real~ sasa_
        -vector~Real~ esolvE_
        +initialize()
        +refresh_energy_cache()
        +store_xyz()
    }
    
    class FACTSRsdTypeInfo {
        -vector~Real~ q_
        -vector~Real~ volume_
        -vector~Real~ COradius2_
        -vector~bool~ not_using_
        +create_info()
        +initialize_parameters()
        +initialize_intrascale()
    }
    
    class FACTSRsdTypeMap {
        -map~ResidueType*, FACTSRsdTypeInfoOP~ type_info_map_
        +get_type_info()
        +restype_destruction_observer()
    }
    
    FACTSPotential -- FACTSRsdTypeMap : uses
    FACTSRsdTypeMap -- FACTSRsdTypeInfo : manages
    FACTSPoseInfo -- FACTSResidueInfo : contains
    FACTSResidueInfo -- FACTSRsdTypeInfo : references
    FACTSPotential -- FACTSPoseInfo : uses
```

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSPotential.hh:47-260](), [source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSResidue.cc:64-475]()

### Core Classes

1. **FACTSPotential**: The main class that provides methods for calculating solvation energies. It handles the setup of the FACTS model for scoring and contains the core algorithms for energy evaluation.

2. **FACTSPoseInfo**: Stores FACTS-related information for an entire pose (molecular structure). It manages a collection of FACTSResidueInfo objects.

3. **FACTSResidueInfo**: Contains FACTS-specific data for individual residues, including calculated values such as Born radii, SASA, and energy components.

4. **FACTSRsdTypeInfo**: Provides residue type-specific parameters and constants needed for FACTS calculations.

5. **FACTSRsdTypeMap**: A database that maps residue types to their corresponding FACTS parameter sets (FACTSRsdTypeInfo).

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSPotential.hh:47-260](), [source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSResidue.cc:64-475](), [source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSResidue.cc:479-507]()

## Calculation Workflow

The FACTS calculation follows a systematic procedure to compute solvation energies:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Setup for Scoring"] --> B["Initialize FACTS Parameters"]
    B --> C["Calculate Burial Terms"]
    C --> D["Calculate Born Radii and SASA"]
    D --> E1["Calculate Polar Energy (Electrostatic)"]
    D --> E2["Calculate Non-Polar Energy (Surface Area)"]
    E1 --> F["Total Solvation Energy"]
    E2 --> F
    
    subgraph "Parameter Initialization"
        B --> B1["Load Atom Type Parameters"]
        B --> B2["Initialize Residue Type Info"]
        B --> B3["Set Enumeration Shell"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Burial Calculation"
        C --> C1["Calculate Ai (Volume)"]
        C --> C2["Calculate Bi (Symmetry)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Self-Term Calculation"
        D --> D1["Calculate Ci and Di Terms"]
        D --> D2["Calculate Born Radii"]
        D --> D3["Calculate SASA"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Energy Evaluation"
        E1 --> E11["Self-Energy Component"]
        E1 --> E12["Pairwise Energy Component"]
        E2 --> E21["Surface Area Component"]
    end
```

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSPotential.cc:138-277](), [source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSPotential.cc:439-503]()

### 1. Setup Phase

When setting up FACTS for scoring, the system follows these steps:

1. **Initialize FACTS Parameters**: Load atom-specific parameters from database files
2. **Set Enumeration Shell**: Determine which residues need recalculation
3. **Store Current Coordinates**: Save the current atomic positions for reference

The setup phase is handled by the `setup_for_scoring` method in the `FACTSPotential` class:

```cpp
void FACTSPotential::setup_for_scoring(pose::Pose & pose, bool const & packing) const
```

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSPotential.cc:138-277]()

### 2. Burial Calculation

The burial calculation determines how buried each atom is within the molecular structure:

1. **Calculate Volume (Ai)**: Compute the volume occupied by surrounding atoms
2. **Calculate Symmetry (Bi)**: Measure the symmetry of the surrounding environment

This is performed by the `res_res_burial_for_scoring` method:

```cpp
void FACTSPotential::res_res_burial_for_scoring(
    conformation::Residue const & rsd1,
    FACTSResidueInfo & facts1,
    conformation::Residue const & rsd2,
    FACTSResidueInfo & facts2
) const
```

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSPotential.cc:348-436]()

### 3. Self-Term Calculation

After burial calculation, the system computes:

1. **Ci Terms**: Combined volume and symmetry terms
2. **Born Radii**: Effective radii for electrostatic calculations
3. **SASA**: Solvent accessible surface area for each atom

This is handled by the `get_self_terms` method:

```cpp
void FACTSPotential::get_self_terms(
    FACTSRsdTypeInfoCOP factstype1,
    FACTSResidueInfo & facts1,
    bool const packing
) const
```

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSPotential.cc:439-503]()

### 4. Energy Calculation

Finally, the system calculates the energy components:

1. **Polar Energy**: Electrostatic interaction with solvent
2. **Non-Polar Energy**: Surface area-based energy contribution

This is performed by `evaluate_polar_energy` and `evaluate_nonpolar_energy` methods.

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSPotential.cc:616-801]()

## Mathematical Model

The FACTS model is based on analytical approximations for calculating solvation energies. The key equations implement:

### Born Radii Calculation

The Born radius represents the effective distance from an atom to the solvent. It is calculated using:

1. **Volume Term (Ai)**: Represents the volume occupied by surrounding atoms
   ```
   Ai = Σj≠i Vj * θij
   ```

2. **Symmetry Term (Bi)**: Measures the asymmetry of the surrounding environment
   ```
   Bi = |Σj≠i (Vj/rij²) * (ri - rj)| / Σj≠i (Vj/rij)
   ```

3. **Combined Term (Ci)**: 
   ```
   Ci = Ai + b1 * Bi + b2 * Ai * Bi
   ```

4. **Born Radius (BR)**: 
   ```
   BR = -0.5 * τ * MultiplicativeFactor / esolvE
   ```

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSPotential.cc:282-345](), [source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSPotential.cc:439-503]()

### Solvent Accessible Surface Area (SASA)

The SASA is calculated using a similar approach:

1. **Combined Term (Di)**:
   ```
   Di = Ai + d1 * Bi + d2 * Ai * Bi
   ```

2. **SASA Calculation**:
   ```
   SASA = c0 + c1/(1 + exp(-c2 * (Di - c3)))
   ```

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSPotential.cc:439-503]()

## Parameter System

FACTS relies on a comprehensive set of parameters for different atom types. These parameters are stored in database files and loaded at runtime.

### Parameter Categories

The main parameter file is `facts_born_params.epm1.txt`, which contains parameters for different atom types:

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| FACTS_RADIUS | Van der Waals radius for the atom |
| FACTS_CUT | Cutoff radius for calculations |
| FACTS_ALPHA | Parameter related to atom polarizability |
| FACTS_B1, FACTS_B2 | Parameters for the Bi term |
| FACTS_D1, FACTS_D2 | Parameters for the Di term |
| FACTS_A0-A3 | Parameters for Born radii calculation |
| FACTS_C0-C3 | Parameters for SASA calculation |

Sources: [database/chemical/atom_type_sets/fa_standard/extras/facts_born_params.epm1.txt:1-57]()

### Parameter Initialization

Parameters are loaded and initialized in the `initialize_parameters` method of `FACTSRsdTypeInfo`:

```cpp
void FACTSRsdTypeInfo::initialize_parameters(chemical::ResidueType const & rsd)
```

This method reads parameters from the atom type set's extra parameters and assigns them to each atom in the residue.

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSResidue.cc:77-266]()

## Configuration Options

FACTS behavior can be customized through several configuration options:

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| facts_kappa | Debye-Hückel screening parameter |
| facts_die | Dielectric constant |
| facts_GBpair_cut | Cutoff for GB pair calculations |
| facts_eq_type | Equation type ("exact", "apprx", "v1trunk") |
| facts_asp_patch | ASP patch version (1, 2, or 3) |
| facts_charge_dir | Directory containing charge parameters |
| facts_saltbridge_correction | Correction factor for salt bridges |

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSPotential.cc:93-135](), [source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSResidue.cc:102-111]()

## Performance Optimizations

FACTS implements several optimizations to improve computational efficiency:

### Multiple Calculation Methods

The system provides three methods for calculating GB pair interactions:

1. **Exact**: Most accurate but computationally expensive
   ```cpp
   void FACTSPotential::calculate_GBpair_exact(...)
   ```

2. **Fast Approximation**: Less accurate but faster
   ```cpp
   void FACTSPotential::calculate_GBpair_fast(...)
   ```

3. **V1 Truncation**: Intermediate approach
   ```cpp
   void FACTSPotential::calculate_GBpair_v1trunk(...)
   ```

The method can be selected using the `facts_eq_type` option.

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSPotential.cc:233-239]()

### Enumeration Shell

FACTS uses an "enumeration shell" concept to avoid recalculating energies for residues that haven't changed:

```cpp
// Set enumeration shell / store current coordinate
for (res1 = 1; res1 <= nres; ++res1) {
    FACTSResidueInfo & facts1(facts_info->residue_info(res1));
    
    if (packing) { // Nothing to take care of; just do full enumeration
        facts1.set_enumeration_shell(true);
    } else { // Scoring, minimizing; refresh energy cache for enumeration shell
        if (facts1.enumeration_shell()) {
            facts1.refresh_energy_cache(nres);
            TR.Debug << " " << res1;
            nshell++;
        }
        facts1.store_xyz(pose.residue(res1));
    }
}
```

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSPotential.cc:162-181]()

## Integration with Scoring System

FACTS is integrated into Rosetta's scoring system as an energy method. It contributes two main terms to the overall score:

1. **facts_elec**: The polar (electrostatic) component
2. **facts_solv**: The polar solvation component 
3. **facts_sasa**: The non-polar (surface area) component

These terms can be weighted in score functions, as shown in the `scorefacts_cart.wts` file:

```
facts_elec 0.25
facts_solv 0.25
facts_sasa 1.0
```

Sources: [database/scoring/weights/scorefacts_cart.wts:5-7]()

## Usage Example

To use FACTS in a Rosetta protocol, you need to:

1. Ensure a score function that includes FACTS terms is selected
2. Configure FACTS-specific options if needed

For example, to use FACTS with a custom dielectric constant:

```
-score:facts_die 20.0
-score:facts_eq_type exact
-score:weights scorefacts_cart
```

## Limitations and Special Cases

The FACTS implementation includes special handling for certain cases:

1. **Charged Hydrogens**: Scaled differently for salt bridges
   ```cpp
   if (factstype1->is_chargedH(atm1)) facts1.BR_[atm1] *= saltbridge_correction_;
   ```

2. **Special Residue Types**: ARG, HIS, TYR, TRP, GLN, ASN have special handling for certain atom pairs
   ```cpp
   if (plane_to_self && rsd.aa() == core::chemical::aa_arg) {
       // Special handling for ARG
   }
   ```

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSPotential.cc:471](), [source/src/core/scoring/facts/FACTSResidue.cc:397-426]()

## Summary

The FACTS Solvation Model provides Rosetta with an efficient and accurate method for calculating solvation energies. It uses analytical approximations to compute Born radii and SASA values, which are then used to calculate polar and non-polar components of the solvation free energy. The implementation is highly optimized and configurable, with special handling for various atom and residue types.

---

This document describes the electron density scoring system in Rosetta, which enables structure modeling and refinement against experimental electron density maps from X-ray crystallography or cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM). For information about setting up density scoring in protocols, see the SetupForDensityScoring mover documentation.

## Overview

The electron density scoring system in Rosetta provides functionality to:

1. Load and manipulate electron density maps
2. Score protein models against these maps
3. Calculate derivatives for optimization
4. Analyze map-model agreement

The core of this functionality is implemented in the `ElectronDensity` class, which handles density map I/O, interpolation, scoring, and gradient calculations.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Core Classes"
        ED["ElectronDensity"]
        XS["OneGaussianScattering"]
        PC["poseCoords"]
    end

    subgraph "Map Processing"
        MAP_IO["Map I/O"]
        FILTER["Reciprocal Space Filtering"]
        SCALE["Scale Map Intensities"]
    end

    subgraph "Scoring Methods"
        RSC["Real Space Correlation"]
        FSC["Fourier Shell Correlation"]
        FAST["Fast Scoring Methods"]
    end

    subgraph "Optimization"
        GRAD["Gradient Calculation"]
        BFAC["B-factor Optimization"]
    end

    ED --> MAP_IO
    ED --> RSC
    ED --> FSC
    ED --> FILTER
    ED --> SCALE
    ED --> GRAD
    GRAD --> BFAC
    RSC --> FAST
    ED --> XS
    PC --> ED
```

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/electron_density/ElectronDensity.hh:54-665](), [source/src/core/scoring/electron_density/ElectronDensity.cc:76-307]()

## Map Representation and Management

### Loading and Accessing Maps

Electron density maps are typically loaded from MRC/CCP4 format files. A singleton pattern is used to maintain a global map instance that can be accessed throughout Rosetta.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant P as Protocol
    participant G as "getDensityMap()"
    participant E as "ElectronDensity"
    
    P->>G: Request map
    G->>E: Load or return existing
    Note over G,E: Singleton pattern
    E->>E: readMRCandResize()
    E->>G: Return map instance
    G->>P: Return map instance
```

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/electron_density/ElectronDensity.cc:127-181](), [source/src/core/scoring/electron_density/ElectronDensity.hh:646-649]()

Key methods for accessing the map:

- `getDensityMap()` - Returns the globally accessible map singleton
- `readMRCandResize()` - Loads a map from disk and optionally resizes it
- `get()` - Retrieves the interpolated density value at a specific point

Once loaded, the map can be accessed and manipulated through the `ElectronDensity` instance. Map data is stored in a 3D array (`ObjexxFCL::FArray3D<float>`) along with metadata about grid dimensions, origin, cell parameters, and resolution.

### Map Processing

Several tools are available for map processing:

- **Scaling**: Adjust map intensities to match theoretical intensities from a model
- **Filtering**: Apply low-pass or high-pass filters in reciprocal space
- **Masking**: Create masks around models for local scoring

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Map Processing Steps"
        LOAD["Load Map"]
        SCALE["Scale Intensities"]
        FILTER["Apply Resolution Filters"]
        MASK["Apply Model Mask"]
        OUTPUT["Output Processed Map"]
    end
    
    LOAD --> SCALE
    SCALE --> FILTER
    FILTER --> MASK
    MASK --> OUTPUT
    
    subgraph "ScaleMapIntensities"
        SMI["ScaleMapIntensities Mover"]
        SMI_RES["Resolution Range"]
        SMI_FADE["Fade Width"]
        SMI_MASK["Mask Options"]
    end
    
    SMI --> SCALE
    SMI --> FILTER
    SMI_RES --> FILTER
    SMI_FADE --> FILTER
    SMI_MASK --> MASK
```

Sources: [source/src/protocols/electron_density/ScaleMapIntensities.cc:46-175](), [source/src/core/scoring/electron_density/ElectronDensity.cc:210-216]()

## Scoring Methods

The electron density module provides several methods to score protein models against density maps, each suited for different use cases.

### Real Space Correlation Calculations

The primary metric used for scoring is the real-space correlation coefficient (CC) between the observed density map and a calculated map generated from the model:

```
CC = (∑ρo·ρc - ∑ρo·∑ρc/n) / √[(∑ρo² - (∑ρo)²/n) · (∑ρc² - (∑ρc)²/n)]
```

Where:
- ρo is the observed density
- ρc is the calculated density
- n is the number of grid points

This calculation is implemented in the `getRSCC()` method.

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/electron_density/ElectronDensity.cc:593-615]()

### Scoring Granularity

The system supports scoring at different levels of granularity:

1. **Whole Structure Scoring**:
   - `matchPose()` - Scores an entire protein against the map
   - `matchCentroidPose()` - Simplified scoring for centroid models

2. **Residue-level Scoring**:
   - `matchRes()` - Scores a specific residue
   - `matchResFast()` - Fast approximation for residue scoring

3. **Atom-level Scoring**:
   - `matchAtomFast()` - Scores a specific atom

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Scoring Methods"
        MP["matchPose()"]
        MCP["matchCentroidPose()"]
        MPP["matchPoseInPocket()"]
        MR["matchRes()"]
        MRF["matchResFast()"]
        MAF["matchAtomFast()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Calculation Flow"
        RHOC["Calculate ρc"]
        MASK["Calculate Mask"]
        STATS["Calculate Statistics"]
        CALC_CC["Calculate CC"]
        DERIVS["Calculate Derivatives"]
    end
    
    MP --> RHOC
    MCP --> RHOC
    MR --> RHOC
    
    RHOC --> MASK
    MASK --> STATS
    STATS --> CALC_CC
    CALC_CC --> DERIVS
    
    subgraph "Used By"
        CART["CartesianSampler"]
        HYBRID["HybridizeProtocol"]
        BFAC["BfactorFittingMover"]
    end
    
    MP --> CART
    MP --> HYBRID
    MRF --> CART
    MR --> BFAC
```

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/electron_density/ElectronDensity.cc:467-670](), [source/src/core/scoring/electron_density/ElectronDensity.cc:676-923](), [source/src/core/scoring/electron_density/ElectronDensity.cc:928-1066]()

### Fast Scoring Methods

For efficiency in iterative optimization, the system includes fast approximations of density scoring:

- Precomputed lookup tables for density values
- Binned B-factor representations
- Spline interpolation for density values

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/electron_density/ElectronDensity.cc:264-425](), [source/src/core/scoring/electron_density/ElectronDensity.hh:582-587]()

## Optimization with Electron Density

### Gradient Calculations

The `ElectronDensity` class provides methods to calculate derivatives of the correlation coefficient with respect to atom positions and B-factors. These derivatives enable optimization of models against the density map.

Key gradient calculation methods:

- `dCCdx_res()` - Calculates CC derivatives with respect to atom positions
- `dCCdx_fastRes()` - Fast approximation of position derivatives
- `dCCdB_fastRes()` - Calculates derivatives with respect to B-factors

The derivatives are used in various minimization protocols to refine structures against experimental density.

Sources: [source/src/core/scoring/electron_density/ElectronDensity.cc:276-298](), [source/src/core/scoring/electron_density/ElectronDensity.hh:276-324]()

### B-factor Optimization

The `BfactorFittingMover` is a specialized mover that optimizes B-factors to improve the fit to the electron density:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "BfactorFittingMover"
        INIT["Initialize B-factors"]
        CC["Calculate Initial CC"]
        MIN["Minimize B-factors"]
        RECC["Recalculate CC"]
    end
    
    INIT --> CC
    CC --> MIN
    MIN --> RECC
    
    subgraph "BfactorMinimizer"
        VARS["Setup Variables"]
        OBJ["Build Objective"]
        GRAD["Calculate Gradients"]
        LP["Linear Programming"]
    end
    
    MIN --> VARS
    VARS --> OBJ
    OBJ --> GRAD
    GRAD --> LP
    
    subgraph "ElectronDensity"
        MATCH["matchRes()"]
        D_CCB["dCCdBs()"]
    end
    
    OBJ --> MATCH
    GRAD --> D_CCB
```

Sources: [source/src/protocols/electron_density/BfactorFittingMover.cc:58-322]()

## Integration with Rosetta Protocols

The electron density scoring functionality is integrated into various Rosetta protocols for structure determination and refinement.

### Setup for Density Scoring

The `SetupForDensityScoringMover` configures a pose for density scoring by:
1. Loading the experimental map
2. Setting up scoring weights
3. Configuring necessary scorefunctions

### Fragment-Based Modeling with Density

The `FragmentBiasAssigner` and `CartesianSampler` classes incorporate density scoring into fragment-based modeling:

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Fragment-Based Modeling"
        CS["CartesianSampler"]
        FBA["FragmentBiasAssigner"]
        FRAG["Fragment Library"]
    end

        ED["ElectronDensity"]

    end
```
